confirmed.title: 「未解決停止」對 AI 的封鎖被 /v1/status 與 interaction.status 工具整份繞過
confirmed.file: crates/interaction-runtime/src/runtime.rs:612-620 (also crates/interaction-api/src/routes.rs:29 `status()` handler and :657 `"interaction.status"` dispatch, both call the same unfiltered `Runtime::status()`)
confirmed.claim: 本分支新增的人類層邊界（agent token 不得讀「哪些感測可能還在擷取、沒人確認停了」）只擋住了 /v1/sensors/unresolved 這一支；同一份紀錄在同一個 commit 裡被原封不動塞進 `Runtime::status()`，而 `GET /v1/status` 與 canonical tool `interaction.status` 都在 agent 白名單內，AI 一次呼叫就拿得到 sourceId／generation／sensors／since／lastKnown／sourceLabel 全欄位。
confirmed.evidence: runtime.rs:610-620 把 `self.unresolved_stops().await` 整包 `serde_json::to_value` 後插進 status 的 `unresolvedStops`（無投影、無遮罩）。interaction-api/src/lib.rs:505-509 的排除條款只有 `!path.starts_with("/v1/sensors/unresolved")`，註解自陳理由是「否則 AI 讀得到一份使用者還沒處理的隱私待辦」；同檔 lib.rs:487-509 的 GET 分支放行 `/v1/status`，lib.rs:531 放行 `POST /v1/tools/*/call`，routes.rs:657 `"interaction.status" => Ok(rt.status().await)`。分支自己的測試把三件事一起釘住：api_e2e.rs:2880-2885 斷言 `status["unresolvedStops"] == listed["unresolvedStops"]`（逐欄相同）、api_e2e.rs:2905-2919 斷言 agent token 讀 /v1/sensors/unresolved 得 403、api_e2e.rs:2922-2929 斷言同一個 agent token 讀 /v1/status 得 200。

verdicts.reasoning:
Verified end-to-end by reading code, not just the diff.

1. `git diff f5b8e2f..HEAD -- crates/interaction-runtime/src/runtime.rs` shows the `unresolved_stops` field and its unconditional splice into `Runtime::status()` (lines ~610-620 in current file: `let unresolved = self.unresolved_stops().await; if !unresolved.is_empty() { ... obj.insert("unresolvedStops", serde_json::to_value(&unresolved)...) }`) are both new in this branch — this is not pre-existing code accidentally caught in the diff.

2. `UnresolvedStop` (crates/interaction-runtime/src/sensor_source.rs:295-309) carries `source_id`, `generation`, `sensors`, `since`, `last_known`, `source_label` — the full record, serialized with no redaction and no principal-awareness.

3. `crates/interaction-api/src/lib.rs`'s `agent_request_allowed` (same branch) blocks agent-token GET on exactly one path — `!path.starts_with("/v1/sensors/unresolved")` — with a comment stating the rationale explicitly: reading this list is a human-layer privacy concern ("否則 AI 讀得到一份使用者還沒處理的隱私待辦"). `/v1/status` is not excluded and matches no other exclusion, so it is allowed for agent tokens.

4. `crates/interaction-api/src/routes.rs::status` is `Json(state.runtime.status().await)` — it doesn't even take an `Extension<AuthContext>` parameter, so the response body is structurally identical regardless of caller (human, legacy agent, session-scoped agent). Same for the canonical tool: `dispatch_tool`'s `"interaction.status" => Ok(rt.status().await)` (routes.rs:657) — the only principal-based tool gating in `tool_call`/`dispatch_tool` targets knowledge tools and `AgentSessionCapability::allows_tool`'s knowledge-specific scoping (crates/interaction-runtime/src/agents.rs:69-85); nothing there touches `interaction.status`, and a plain `LegacyAgent` bearer token (the kind used throughout the test suite) isn't scope-checked for it at all.

5. Ran the branch's own test `unresolved_stops_are_listed_and_only_a_human_can_dismiss_one` (`cargo test -p interaction-api --test api_e2e unresolved_stops_are_listed_and_only_a_human_can_dismiss_one`) — passes. Its own assertions and comments corroborate the bug rather than refute it: it checks `GET /v1/sensors/unresolved` returns 403 for the agent token, then separately checks `GET /v1/status` returns 200 for the agent token with the comment "這條排除只涵蓋 unresolved 這一支：agent 平面其餘的讀取不受影響" (this exclusion only covers the unresolved endpoint; the rest of the agent plane is unaffected) — but it never asserts the agent-token status response's *body content*, so the test suite never notices that the identical `unresolvedStops` payload rides along on the very endpoint it deliberately leaves open. Earlier in the same test, `status["unresolvedStops"] == listed["unresolvedStops"]` is asserted (with the *human* token) to prove the two read surfaces show the same fact — which, combined with point 4's principal-blind handler code, proves the agent-token `/v1/status` call gets that same array too.

6. Checked `docs/aip/privacy.md` §5.1 (the design doc for this exact feature, in this branch): it justifies blocking the *dismiss* path as human-layer ("這是人類層動作：agent token 打不到這條路徑") and separately notes "status 已經帶著這個欄位，前端還沒讀它" — i.e. the team knew `status` carries the field for desktop/tray consumption, but nowhere claims or defends that this is also symmetric with the deliberate agent-read block on `/v1/sensors/unresolved`. No mention of this gap exists in CHANGELOG.md, docs/acceptance-evidence.md, or the v0.6.x progress doc — it is not a documented/accepted known limitation, it's an unnoticed inconsistency between two access-control lists written in the same commit.

This is a real, reproducible defect: the human-only read boundary that the team explicitly built and tested for "unresolved sensor stop" data is completely undermined by the exact same payload riding unfiltered through two other already-agent-accessible surfaces (`GET /v1/status`, canonical tool `interaction.status`) that were not updated when the privacy-sensitive field was added to the shared `status()` builder.

Line-number nit: the finding's header cites `runtime.rs:611`; the actual anchor lines in the current file are 612 (`let unresolved = self.unresolved_stops().await;`) and 616 (`"unresolvedStops".into()`) — a 1-2 line drift, immaterial to the claim, which the finding's own "evidence" field already correctly ranges as 610-620.

Verified end-to-end, no refutation found.

1. `Runtime::status()` (crates/interaction-runtime/src/runtime.rs:610-620) unconditionally serializes the full `unresolved_stops()` list (sourceId, generation, sensors, since, lastKnown, sourceLabel) into `unresolvedStops` whenever the set is non-empty — no principal parameter, no projection, no redaction.

2. `agent_request_allowed` (crates/interaction-api/src/lib.rs:487-509) excludes only `!path.starts_with("/v1/sensors/unresolved")` for GET, with a comment stating the exact rationale the claim quotes verbatim: "讀取面也必須同一層，否則 AI 讀得到一份使用者還沒處理的隱私待辦" — and explicitly notes "只排除這一支：`/v1/sensors`（狀態）… 不受影響". `/v1/status` is not excluded and `/v1/tools/*/call` is affirmatively allowed a few lines later.

3. `dispatch_tool`'s `"interaction.status" => Ok(rt.status().await)` (crates/interaction-api/src/routes.rs:657) applies no additional filtering. For `AuthPrincipal::LegacyAgent` the match arm at routes.rs:630-634 only gates knowledge tools; there is no `allows_tool` scoping for LegacyAgent at all, so a plain agent token gets the unfiltered result. Even a scoped `AgentSession` merely needs `interaction.status` in its tool_scope (a generically useful, non-privileged-sounding capability) to get the same result — `allows_tool` does no content-level filtering.

4. The commit that added the exclusion (9799b1ea) also added its own regression test asserting the opposite of the claimed protection: `crates/interaction-api/src/lib.rs` `agent_token_cannot_read_the_unresolved_stops_inbox` explicitly asserts `agent_request_allowed(&Method::GET, "/v1/status")` is `true` ("其餘 GET 不受影響"). And `crates/interaction-api/tests/api_e2e.rs:2870-2920` independently proves the live behavior: agent token gets 403 on `/v1/sensors/unresolved` but 200 on `/v1/status`, and directly before that asserts `status["unresolvedStops"] == listed["unresolvedStops"]` — i.e. the test suite documents, rather than catches, the exact bypass the claim describes.

5. Checked CHANGELOG [Unreleased] and `docs/releases/v0.6.x-maintainability-progress.md` for any acknowledgment of this as an accepted/known gap — found none. The commit message for 9799b1e frames the `/v1/sensors/unresolved` exclusion as *closing* a privacy gap ("同一支分支順手收掉 M3 的兩個誠實缺口"), not as a partial/best-effort mitigation, so this isn't a documented known limitation — it's an unnoticed hole in a fix that believed itself complete.

This is a real, self-contradicting boundary defect: the developer's own stated security rationale ("AI 不得讀到使用者還沒處理的隱私待辦") is defeated by an alternate, in-scope, agent-reachable read path carrying byte-identical data, and the branch's own tests lock in rather than catch the gap. `source_id` is explicitly commented elsewhere in the same file (sensor_source.rs:305-307) as "內部識別，一般模式不得顯示" and `generation` is a monotonic per-registration counter — both are exactly the class of shared-state identifiers the project's invariants care about not exposing across this trust boundary. Severity: I keep it at high (not blocker) since the leaked payload is metadata about an unconfirmed sensor stop, not live sensor content or a credential/consent-granting capability, and it requires an already-issued agent token to exploit — but it is a genuine, verifiable violation of a boundary the same commit explicitly set out to build, not a style nit or already-mitigated concern.

Line drift: the runtime.rs line cited in the finding (611) is off by one from the current file (the `let unresolved = self.unresolved_stops().await;` statement is at line 612); everything else in the evidence trail (lib.rs:505-509, routes.rs:657, api_e2e.rs:2870-2920) matches current file contents exactly.

confirmed.fix: status() 不再攜帶完整紀錄（只留一個不含識別碼的計數／布林，或整段移除，讓桌面改打人類層端點）；若要保留完整欄位，就必須在 handler 依 AuthPrincipal 遮罩，並把 `interaction.status` 的工具輸出走同一條遮罩。再補一支測試：agent token 讀 /v1/status 與呼叫 interaction.status 都看不到 unresolvedStops。
confirmed.regressionTest: In crates/interaction-api/tests/api_e2e.rs, extend `unresolved_stops_are_listed_and_only_a_human_can_dismiss_one` (or add a new test) to actually parse the agent-token `/v1/status` response body — not just its status code — and assert `!body.get("unresolvedStops").is_some_and(...)` or that it's redacted/absent for `AuthPrincipal::LegacyAgent`/`AgentSession`; add the same assertion for a `POST /v1/tools/interaction.status/call` made with `server.agent_token`. Fix direction: project `unresolvedStops` (and any other field carrying human-layer detail) out of the JSON returned by `routes::status` and by the `"interaction.status"` tool branch whenever the caller's `AuthPrincipal` isn't `Human`/a session capability scoped for it — mirroring the same exclusion already applied to the dedicated `/v1/sensors/unresolved` route — rather than only gating the single-purpose endpoint. / In crates/interaction-api/tests/api_e2e.rs, extend the existing orphan-stop fixture (the one at ~line 2840-2920 that already creates an unresolved stop and reads /v1/sensors/unresolved + /v1/status with the agent token): after confirming `/v1/sensors/unresolved` returns 403 for the agent token, assert the *content* of the still-200 `/v1/status` response does NOT contain `unresolvedStops` for agent/legacy-agent principals (e.g. by having `Runtime::status()` take a principal/visibility flag and omitting the field unless the caller is Human), and add a matching assertion for `POST /v1/tools/interaction.status/call` with `server.agent_token` — today both would need to change from 'field present' to 'field absent' once fixed. Also add an assertion in the `interaction-api::lib::auth_scope_tests` module mirroring `agent_token_cannot_read_the_unresolved_stops_inbox` but checking that a status *payload* fetched via the agent token lacks the key, not just that the path-level gate passes — a path-level boolean test alone cannot catch a same-content leak via a different, allowed path.

confirmed.title: 重新綁定握手逾時後，新建的裝置線永遠被生命週期閘門拒收，provider 卻仍會收斂成 Available
confirmed.file: crates/interaction-runtime/src/declarative_lifecycle.rs:630 (handshake-timeout branch of run_declarative_rebind); root cause spans providers.rs:810-821 (bind_declarative_device + note_declarative_bound during step 7) and declarative_lifecycle.rs:410-439 (fail_declarative_rebind never tears down what step 7 built)
confirmed.claim: rebind 第 7 步已經重新註冊 spec（開了新連線、spawn 了新的 DeviceBinding task、登記了新的 SensorSource），第 7 步後半等握手時逾時就 `return Err(RebindStop::Failed)`，於是 `settle_declarative_rebind(false)` 把 lifecycle 寫成 `Unbound{Disconnected}`——但沒有任何路徑收掉那批新 task。裝置晚一點插回來時，`note_ready` 會把 provider 從 Disconnected 收斂成 Available、登記出站通道、presence 轉 Online，而 `on_aip` 的閘門看到 lifecycle != Bound，會把這台裝置之後的**每一則** AIP frame 丟掉。畫面說「可用、已連線」，實際上這台裝置從此一句話都送不進來，且只有再按一次「啟用」或重啟 daemon 才救得回。
confirmed.evidence: declarative_lifecycle.rs:596-598 在鎖內呼叫 `rt.register_declarative_spec(&spec)`（→ providers.rs:806-821 `bind_declarative_device` spawn 連線 task ＋ `register_sensor_source`，並 `note_declarative_bound`，但因 lifecycle 是 `Rebinding` 而**不**寫成 Bound，見 declarative_lifecycle.rs:152-160）；declarative_lifecycle.rs:616-637 的握手等待在逾時／`LinkReadiness::Closed` 時直接 return Err；declarative_lifecycle.rs:404-430 `fail_declarative_rebind` 只呼叫 `settle_declarative_rebind(..., false)`（:316-334 寫成 `Unbound{Disconnected}`）＋改 detail＋留稽核，沒有 `tasks.abort_all()`／`close_declarative_links`／`unregister_sensor_source`。declarative_session.rs:379-395 的 `run()` 迴圈用 500 ms→15 s 退避無限重試 `ensure_ready()`，成功就進 `note_ready`（:164-198），其中 :196 呼叫 `converge_provider_after_rebind`（providers.rs:1431-1444：只要 state == Disconnected 就翻成 Available）。declarative_session.rs:258-274 的閘門 `if lifecycle != DeclarativeLifecycle::Bound { audit "aip.rejected"; return; }`。全域只有兩處寫 Bound：providers.rs:821 的 `note_declarative_bound` 與 declarative_lifecycle.rs:645 的 `settle_declarative_rebind(true)`。既有測試 declarative_session_loop.rs:1700-1706 已經釘住「逾時後 lifecycle == Unbound{Disconnected}」，缺的是「之後裝置連上來還算不算數」。

verdicts.reasoning:
Traced the whole rebind path and it holds up exactly as claimed, no line drift on any of the load-bearing citations.

1. Step 7 of run_declarative_rebind (declarative_lifecycle.rs:590-610) calls rt.register_declarative_spec(&spec) while lifecycle is still Rebinding{generation}. That call (providers.rs:738-880) does real, live work: it opens new serial/mqtt/ble connections, calls bind_declarative_device (providers.rs:810-816, declarative_session.rs:798-838) which spawns a fresh DeviceBinding per channel (declarative_session.rs:806-817) and registers a brand-new DeclarativeSensorSource (declarative_session.rs:819-830), then calls note_declarative_bound (providers.rs:821) which — per its own explicit guard at declarative_lifecycle.rs:157-159 — does NOT flip lifecycle to Bound while a Rebinding entry is in progress, by design.

2. Each spawned DeviceBinding.run() (declarative_session.rs:374-448) loops forever calling channel.ensure_ready() with 500ms→15s backoff (HANDSHAKE_BACKOFF_MIN/MAX, declarative_session.rs:55-56) — this loop has no total deadline; it only stops when the channel's readiness becomes Closed or the runtime is dropped.

3. run_declarative_rebind's own wait (declarative_lifecycle.rs:612-639) polls the same channel objects but is bounded by REBIND_HANDSHAKE_BUDGET = 20s. If the device is slower than that, it hits the deadline check at line 630 and returns Err(RebindStop::Failed(...)).

4. That propagates to fail_declarative_rebind (declarative_lifecycle.rs:410-439), which only calls settle_declarative_rebind(..., false) (→ Unbound{Disconnected}, lines 316-334) plus note_provider_rebind_failed (providers.rs:1458-1487, which keeps ProviderState at Disconnected with a rebind-failed note) and an audit row. It never calls close_declarative_links, never aborts the TaskGroup that bind_declarative_device just created, never unregisters the DeclarativeSensorSource registered in step 7. So the DeviceBinding tasks and the new DeclarativeSensorSource from the failed attempt keep running, orphaned.

5. If the device connects later, the orphaned DeviceBinding.run()'s ensure_ready() succeeds and calls note_ready() (declarative_session.rs:164-198), which registers the outbound channel, flips presence Online, and — at line 196 — calls converge_provider_after_rebind (providers.rs:1431-1451). That function's only gate is `existing.state == Disconnected` (providers.rs:1434-1435); it does not check declarative_lifecycle at all, and it strips the rebind-failed note from detail (it filters is_rebind_note out of warnings before writing), so the descriptor now shows a clean Available with no visible trace of the earlier failure.

6. Meanwhhile lifecycle is still stuck at Unbound{Disconnected} — the only two writers of Bound are note_declarative_bound (providers.rs:821, which explicitly refuses to write Bound while Rebinding, per point 1) and settle_declarative_rebind(..., true) (declarative_lifecycle.rs:645, only reached by the code path that already returned Err before this device's own success arrives). So DeviceBinding::on_aip's gate (declarative_session.rs:259-275, `if lifecycle != Bound { audit aip.rejected; return; }`) now rejects every subsequent frame from this device, forever — while the provider descriptor and character-session presence both say the device is there and reachable.

7. Confirmed this is a real gap, not already covered: the only existing test on this path, rebind_timeout_is_bounded_and_honest (declarative_session_loop.rs, using dead_spec pointed at a serial path that never exists), only asserts the post-timeout state (lifecycle Unbound{Disconnected}, ProviderState Disconnected) — it never brings the device online afterward, so it cannot see the orphaned-task/converge-without-Bound sequence. I also checked docs/aip/device-profile.md §6.1 (added in this same branch, commit 2aad4dd) and docs/releases/v0.7.0-drills.md §4 — both document that `Bound` isn't itself exposed via API and that Bound doesn't strictly mean handshake success, and the drill only exercised the happy path (reconnect inside the 20s/1s budget) — neither documents or covers this specific failure-then-late-success divergence between ProviderState and DeclarativeLifecycle. So this is a genuine, previously unacknowledged bug, not a known/documented limitation.

The recovery claim also checks out: since lifecycle is Unbound{Disconnected} (rebindable() == true), a human-initiated Disabled→Available cycle re-enters begin_declarative_rebind and redoes the 8 steps from scratch (closing the orphaned links this time via close_declarative_links, which operates on the provider's registered links regardless of which "generation" of channel object opened them), which is consistent with "只有再按一次「啟用」或重啟 daemon 才救得回."

I rate this "high" (matches the reporter): it is a silent, total loss of inbound communication with a device the UI/API represent as connected/online — a serious honesty-ladder violation (ProviderState no longer reflects real connectivity, and the divergence is invisible through any documented surface) — but it is not a crash, data-loss, or unrecoverable condition, and a known two-step manual recovery (disable → enable) exists, so I did not escalate to "blocker."</reasoning>
<regression_test_sketch">Extend rebind_timeout_is_bounded_and_honest (or add a sibling test) using the pty Fixture instead of dead_spec: start the rebind, let it hit the 20s handshake timeout and settle to Unbound{Disconnected}/rebind-failed (as the existing test already does), then — after the failure is observed — bring the fixture's serial link up (satisfy its hello/pairing so ensure_ready() succeeds) and wait_until provider_state(&rt, &pid) becomes Available again. Assert that when that happens, rt.declarative_lifecycle(pid.as_str()) is NOT DeclarativeLifecycle::Bound, and that sending a frame from the fixture after that point produces an aip.rejected{reason:"this device's binding is not established"} audit row instead of being processed — proving the provider shows Available while remaining permanently deaf until a manual disable/enable.</regression_test_sketch>

Traced the whole path with the current file contents (this module is entirely new in this branch: crates/interaction-runtime/src/declarative_lifecycle.rs was added by b32ba10, 695 lines, 0 before).

1. Step 7 of run_declarative_rebind (declarative_lifecycle.rs:583-609) calls rt.register_declarative_spec(&spec) while holding the provider lock. That call (providers.rs:738-873) spawns real transport connections, registers receptors/actuators, and — critically — calls bind_declarative_device (providers.rs:797-804 → declarative_session.rs:798-833), which spawns a brand-new `TaskGroup` of independent `DeviceBinding::run()` tokio tasks and registers a brand-new `DeclarativeSensorSource` via `register_sensor_source`. `note_declarative_bound` (providers.rs:821, declarative_lifecycle.rs:131-169) records the new channels but explicitly refuses to flip lifecycle to `Bound` while it is `Rebinding` (declarative_lifecycle.rs:152-160) — by design, so a later failure isn't hidden.

2. The handshake-wait loop back in run_declarative_rebind (declarative_lifecycle.rs:611-635) is a *separate, passive poll* of `channel.handshake_ready()`/`readiness()` — it does not drive the connection itself. The actual connecting/retrying is done by the already-spawned, independent `DeviceBinding::run()` task (declarative_session.rs:374-420), which loops forever with its own 500 ms→15 s backoff, checking only `LinkReadiness::Closed` or runtime-drop as exit conditions — completely decoupled from the rebind's 20 s handshake budget or 40 s total budget.

3. On timeout, declarative_lifecycle.rs:628-633 returns `Err(RebindStop::Failed(...))`. `fail_declarative_rebind` (declarative_lifecycle.rs:410-437) only calls `settle_declarative_rebind(..., false)`, which writes `Unbound{Disconnected}` (declarative_lifecycle.rs:316-334) and audits `provider.rebind-failed`. It never calls `close_declarative_links`, never aborts the new `TaskGroup`, and never unregisters the new `DeclarativeSensorSource`. `note_provider_rebind_failed` (providers.rs:1457-1486) leaves the ProviderState at `existing.state`, i.e. still `Disconnected` — the exact precondition `converge_provider_after_rebind` checks for.

4. So the orphaned `DeviceBinding::run()` task keeps retrying indefinitely in the background. If the physical device later becomes reachable on its own (replug, broker restart, BLE back in range), `ensure_ready()` succeeds and `note_ready()` fires (declarative_session.rs:164-198). `note_ready` unconditionally registers the outbound channel, flips presence to Online if already a member, and — unconditionally, with no lifecycle check at all — calls `rt.converge_provider_after_rebind(...)` (providers.rs:1425-1449), which only checks `existing.state == Disconnected` (true) and flips ProviderState to `Available`.

5. Meanwhile `declarative_lifecycle` is still `Unbound{Disconnected}` — nothing anywhere sets it back to `Bound` except `note_declarative_bound` (only called from `register_declarative_spec`, i.e. a fresh explicit rebind/restart) and `settle_declarative_rebind(true)` (only on the *same* rebind's own success path, already consumed as `false`). I grepped every reference to `declarative_lifecycle`/`Bound` writers (providers.rs, declarative_session.rs, declarative_lifecycle.rs) and found no reconciliation path.

6. `on_aip` (declarative_session.rs:258-274) gates every subsequent inbound AIP frame on `lifecycle == Bound` and otherwise audits `aip.rejected`/"this device's binding is not established" and drops it — silently from the user's point of view (only an internal audit row, no UI signal), while the UI/provider descriptor says Available/Online.

7. Confirmed the existing regression test `rebind_timeout_is_bounded_and_honest` (declarative_session_loop.rs:1622-1701) uses `dead_spec`, which points at a nonexistent socket path that can *never* succeed — so it only proves the immediate failed state, and structurally cannot exercise "the device reconnects after the rebind gave up," which is exactly the scenario this finding describes. No other test covers it either.

This is a genuine, newly-introduced gap in this branch's headline feature (background rebind), not a style nit, not already covered by tests, and not superseded by any other mechanism I could find. It represents a real honesty-ladder violation (ProviderState/presence claim Available/Online while the device is functionally deaf) and a resource-lifecycle leak (orphaned task group/SensorSource never retired on rebind failure) that only a manual re-enable or daemon restart repairs, matching the finding's exact narrative and evidence chain.

confirmed.fix: rebind 失敗時把第 7 步建立的東西一起收掉（retire 新的 DeclarativeSensorSource ＋ close_declarative_links），讓下一次連線走乾淨的重建；或改成握手成功由 `note_ready` 回頭 settle（成功即 Bound），失敗只保留「還沒連上」而不把已經活著的綁定標成 Unbound。另加測試：dead port → rebind 逾時 → 之後 pty 模擬器上線 → 裝置的 capability frame 必須被接受（且不得只靠外部重試掩蓋）。

verdicts.reasoning:
Read every piece of the chain end to end and it holds exactly as claimed:

1. `DeclarativeSensorSource::request_stop` (declarative_session.rs:656-679) computes `targets` from `enabled_high_risk()` (registry flags only) plus this *instance's own* `stop_pending` map. When both are empty it returns at line 679 `AlreadyStopped` covering `self.high_risk.clone()` — the whole declared high-risk family for this provider — with `waited_ms: 0`, before ever reaching `self.channels`/`channel.stop_all()`. Verified this exact branch is byte-for-byte unchanged from the base commit (f5b8e2f) — `git show f5b8e2f:.../declarative_session.rs` has the identical `if targets.is_empty() { ... AlreadyStopped ... }` at the same lines.

2. `SensorStopStatus::confirmed()` (sensor_source.rs, pre-existing) treats `AlreadyStopped` the same as `Stopped`.

3. `stop_all_sensor_sources` (sensors.rs:536-544) collects `confirmed` sensors from any report where `r.confirmed()` and calls `resolve_stops_for(source.source_id(), &confirmed)` for every currently-registered source, unconditionally.

4. `resolve_stops_for` (sensor_source.rs:637-690) — **new in this branch** (baseline has no `resolve_stops_for`, `UnresolvedStop`, or generation-keyed `SourceKey` at all) — filters `unresolved_stops`/`orphan_captures` by `source_id` alone (`.filter(|(id, _)| id == source_id)`), with **no generation check**, removes any matching sensors from every generation's entry, deletes the entry once empty, and writes `sensor.unresolved-stop-resolved`.

Because `bind_declarative_device` (called from providers.rs on every build/rebind) always constructs a brand-new `DeclarativeSensorSource` with a fresh, empty `stop_pending: Mutex::new(BTreeMap::new())` (declarative_session.rs ~824-828), a rebind after a disconnect produces exactly the scenario described: a new generation with nothing enabled and nothing pending, which fabricates an `AlreadyStopped` over the whole family with zero device communication, and that fabricated confirmation is then used by the new cross-generation `resolve_stops_for` to erase an older generation's genuinely unresolved stop.

This is precisely the situation `SourceKey`'s own doc comment (sensor_source.rs ~44-50) says must not happen ("新來源不知道舊連線那一頭發生過什麼事，抹掉等於用一台新裝置替一台舊裝置作證") and that `UnresolvedStop`'s doc comment (~277-283) says can only be cleared by "明確的確認或人為解除" — an empty-targets fast path that never touches a channel is neither.

I built a standalone reproduction outside the repo (temp crate at /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/verify_sensor, path-depending on the real `interaction-core`/`interaction-runtime` crates, compiled with the repo's real target dir so it links the actual current code — no repo files were created or modified) that: registers a genuinely-stuck source (gen1, active capture, `request_stop` times out → Unknown), unregisters it while still "active" so it orphans, advances `rt.sensor_clock` past `ORPHAN_CAPTURE_VISIBLE` so it settles into `UnresolvedStop(gen1)`, then registers a second, unrelated source under the *same* `source_id` whose `active_captures()` is always empty and whose `request_stop` fabricates `AlreadyStopped` over the declared family without ever touching any device-contact field (mirroring `DeclarativeSensorSource`'s empty-targets branch), then calls the real `rt.stop_all_sensor_sources(...)` (the exact function both the "Stop All Sensors" button and emergency stop use).

Result, actually run:
```
sweep reports: [... { source_id: "fixture.declarative-device", ..., outcome: AlreadyStopped, waited_ms: 0, ... }]
unresolved after sweep: []
audit kinds: ["sensor.unresolved-stop-resolved", "sensor.stop-requested", "sensor.unresolved-stop-recorded", "sensor.source-removed-while-capturing"]
test ... ok
```

The gen1 `UnresolvedStop` — which represented a real, still-unconfirmed stop request to a device that never acknowledged it — was silently wiped and audited as `sensor.unresolved-stop-resolved`, driven entirely by a second registration that never communicated with any device. This is fully reproducible, not timing-dependent, and reachable through completely ordinary operation (device disconnects mid-capture without ack → provider gets disabled/retired → 60s pass → provider is re-enabled/rebound, with the high-risk receptor defaulting back to requires-consent/off per the repo's own default-off invariant → user clicks "Stop All Sensors" or triggers emergency stop, both of which share `stop_all_sensor_sources`).

I bump severity from medium to high: this is a deterministic, always-reproducible violation of an explicitly documented, just-introduced safety/honesty invariant (the whole point of adding generation-tracked `UnresolvedStop` in this branch was to prevent exactly this "new source vouches for old" erasure), triggered by ordinary use rather than an exotic race. It does not reach "blocker" because the corruption is confined to the retired-generation diagnostic/audit trail (`unresolvedStops`, its accompanying audit log, and any UI that surfaces it for human dismissal) rather than the currently-registered source's live `activeSensors` visibility or an actual consent-gate bypass — the live sensor stays correctly gated off in the new generation.

verdicts.reasoning: Traced the full path end to end in the current tree (all in this branch's new files; declarative_lifecycle.rs is wholly new via commit b32ba10). (1) providers.rs:1431 `converge_provider_after_rebind` transitions state Disconnected→Available whenever called, gated ONLY on `existing.state == Disconnected` — no lifecycle check anywhere in its body (verified lines 1431-1455). It also filters out `rebind-failed:`/`rebinding:` warnings via `is_rebind_note` (providers.rs:1731-1733), erasing the failure explanation. (2) declarative_session.rs:158-197 `DeviceBinding::note_ready` calls this unconditionally every time `channel.ensure_ready()` succeeds inside `DeviceBinding::run()`'s retry loop (line 808/816 spawns this loop with its own unbounded backoff up to 15s, independent of any rebind generation/budget). (3) The `on_aip` gate (declarative_session.rs:259-261) hard-rejects every inbound frame when `declarative_lifecycle(provider_id) != Bound`. (4) declarative_lifecycle.rs confirms lifecycle is set to `Bound` in exactly three places: init on first-ever registration (line 147), `note_declarative_bound` guarded to skip while `Rebinding` (line 156-159, only called once per rebind attempt from `register_declarative_spec`, not on every handshake success), and `settle_declarative_rebind(ok=true)` (line 326), which is scoped to the *same generation* inside `run_declarative_rebind` and is never invoked again after that task exits. (5) `run_declarative_rebind`'s own handshake wait (lines 616-638) times out after REBIND_HANDSHAKE_BUDGET=20s and, on timeout, calls `fail_declarative_rebind`→`settle_declarative_rebind(gen,false)`, setting lifecycle to `Unbound{Disconnected}` (line 316-334) — this is a *different, independent* clock/loop from the DeviceBinding task's own indefinite retry-with-backoff loop, which has no absolute deadline. So a device whose full hello/pairing handshake takes longer than 20s (plausible: slow boot after DTR reset, broker reconnect backoff, BLE re-pairing) will cause: t=20s rebind declared Failed (lifecycle→Unbound{Disconnected}, state stays Disconnected with an honest 'rebind-failed' warning) while the still-running DeviceBinding task keeps retrying; when it later succeeds (t>20s), `note_ready`→`converge_provider_after_rebind` flips state to Available and scrubs the rebind-failed warning, but nothing ever touches lifecycle back to Bound. From that point every `on_aip` frame from this device is rejected (audited, but not surfaced in UI) forever, while status shows a clean Available provider. Only path out is `begin_declarative_rebind`, reachable solely via providers.rs:1365 inside `transition_provider`, i.e. a human re-triggering enable — exactly as claimed. Checked `rebind_timeout_is_bounded_and_honest` (tests/declarative_session_loop.rs:1625) and it only asserts the failure moment using a `dead_spec` pointing at a nonexistent serial port (transport never even opens), so it can never exercise 'device connects after the 20s budget already expired' — confirming the claim that this path is untested. Grepped for any reconciliation/health-check that syncs state vs lifecycle: none exists. All file/line citations in the finding match the current tree exactly, with no drift.

Verified the entire call chain against current file content with no line drift:

1. providers.rs:1431 `converge_provider_after_rebind` only guards on `existing.state != ProviderState::Disconnected { return; }` — never reads `DeclarativeLifecycle`.
2. declarative_session.rs:164-196 `DeviceBinding::note_ready` calls it unconditionally whenever `channel.ensure_ready()` succeeds inside `DeviceBinding::run()`'s retry loop (no lifecycle gate at the call site either).
3. `DeviceBinding::run()` tasks are spawned in `bind_declarative_device` (declarative_session.rs:808-816) as part of step 7 of `run_declarative_rebind` (declarative_lifecycle.rs, called via `register_declarative_spec`), independently of the subsequent 20s handshake-ready poll in step 8 (declarative_lifecycle.rs:611-638).
4. On timeout, `RebindStop::Failed` -> `fail_declarative_rebind` (declarative_lifecycle.rs:410) -> `settle_declarative_rebind(...,false)` (line 316) sets lifecycle to `Unbound{Disconnected}`, and `note_provider_rebind_failed` (providers.rs:1457) writes the `rebind-failed: reason` warning while leaving ProviderState at `Disconnected`. Neither function touches the newly-spawned `DeviceBinding` task or its channel (`close_declarative_links` is only ever called on `previous` channels or on explicit disable/revoke — grepped all call sites, confirmed).
5. That orphaned task keeps looping (`ensure_ready()` retry with backoff); its only exit condition is `LinkReadiness::Closed`, which the failure path never sets. If the device later actually completes handshake, `note_ready()` fires, unconditionally converging ProviderState back to `Available` and filtering the `rebind-failed`/`rebinding` notes via `is_rebind_note` (providers.rs:1731).
6. `DeclarativeLifecycle` is never re-synced on this late success (no code path calls `note_declarative_bound`/`settle_declarative_rebind` from `note_ready`), so it stays `Unbound{Disconnected}` permanently. `on_aip`'s gate (declarative_session.rs:259-261) checks exactly this lifecycle and rejects every frame with `lifecycle != Bound` — so the device is durably cut off from Character Session while the UI/tray honestly-worded provider state claims `Available` with no warning.
7. Confirmed the existing test `rebind_timeout_is_bounded_and_honest` (tests/declarative_session_loop.rs:1625) only checks state immediately after the failure and then exercises a *new* manual re-enable (new generation) — it never exercises the original failed attempt's channel succeeding afterward, so this exact interleaving is genuinely untested.

This is a real divergence between two independent state owners (ProviderState vs DeclarativeLifecycle) for the same physical connection, violating the honesty-ladder invariant (state must not outrun/contradict actual binding) and silently, durably breaking device I/O while reporting success — recoverable only by a further manual disable/enable cycle, exactly as claimed.

Assert the bug: `provider_state(&rt, &pid)` becomes `Available` again (state lies), while `rt.declarative_lifecycle(pid.as_str())` stays `Unbound{Disconnected}` (or at least != Bound), and a synthetic `aip` frame sent on that channel is rejected via an `aip.rejected` audit row with reason "this device's binding is not established" even though the provider shows Available. The fix should either (a) have `converge_provider_after_rebind` also check/require `DeclarativeLifecycle::Bound` (or transition it to Bound atomically) before flipping state to Available, and/or (b) abort the orphaned `DeviceBinding`/channel task when a rebind attempt fails, so a late handshake from a stale attempt can never resurrect the provider.

(2) rebind step 7 (declarative_lifecycle.rs:595-608) reads that record, re-registers the full spec via register_declarative_spec (which — per interaction-registry/src/lib.rs:114-128 register_receptor — always inserts freshly with `enabled: !manifest.requires_consent`, i.e. non-consent receptors default to enabled, and errors on double-registration so a prior disabled entry can't survive), re-applies set_receptor_enabled(false) for the recorded ids, and only THEN unconditionally clears the record — all before returning to wait on the up-to-20s handshake outside the lock. (3) If that handshake never completes, run_declarative_rebind returns RebindStop::Failed; note_provider_rebind_failed (providers.rs:1457-1483) only rewrites the state/detail warning, touching no receptor flags, and settle_declarative_rebind moves the lifecycle to Unbound{Disconnected} (rebindable()==true per declarative_lifecycle.rs:77-80). At this point the receptor is still correctly off (attempt #1's own re-disable already took effect on the registry), but the human_disabled record is already empty. (4) A second transition_provider(Available) does not re-derive human_disabled (Available isn't provider_stopped), it just calls begin_declarative_rebind -> enter_declarative_rebinding -> a second run_declarative_rebind. Its step 6 unregisters the (currently disabled) receptor as an old capability giving way; step 7 reads human_disabled — now empty — and register_declarative_spec reinstalls it at the manifest default enabled=true, with no set_receptor_enabled(false) left to counter it. Net effect: a receptor a human deliberately turned off is silently turned back on after a failed-then-retried rebind, with no human action in between — a direct violation of the branch's own stated guarantee that returning to Available never restores any capability. Cross-checked against tests/declarative_session_loop.rs: `rebind_keeps_human_disabled_receptors_off` (line 1949) only exercises a single successful rebind (real pty simulator that completes the handshake) and never induces a failure; `rebind_timeout_is_bounded_and_honest` (line 1624) induces exactly the failure+retry sequence described but uses a spec with no non-consent receptor and never asserts receptor-enabled state after the retry. Neither test, nor any other in the file (grep for 'human_disabled' found only that one test), covers the combination, so the gap is real and unguarded. All line numbers cited in the finding (declarative_lifecycle.rs:595-611, providers.rs:1286-1315, 1364-1367, 77-80; interaction-registry/src/lib.rs:128) matched the current file content exactly — not stale, not already fixed. Did not add a live reproduction test to the repo since the task instructions forbid modifying/creating any files during this review; the static trace is unambiguous and every write site to human_disabled_receptors in the crate was enumerated (exactly one), so no other code path can repopulate the record between the two rebind attempts.

Traced the full control flow and it holds up.

1. `note_declarative_human_disabled` (the only writer of `human_disabled_receptors`) is called exactly once, in `providers.rs` inside `if provider_stopped(state)` (disable/close/expire/revoke path only — confirmed at providers.rs:1286-1315). It is never called on the enable path.

2. `run_declarative_rebind` (declarative_lifecycle.rs:458-668) is the *only* place that reads (`declarative_human_disabled`, line 595) and clears (`clear_declarative_human_disabled`, line 608) that list, and it runs in full on *every* rebind attempt, including a retry after a prior failure — this is explicitly exercised by the existing test `rebind_timeout_is_bounded_and_honest` (declarative_session_loop.rs:1624-1706), which shows `transition_provider(Available)` on a `Disconnected` provider (after a failed rebind) starts a brand-new `run_declarative_rebind` from step 1, and the code comments themselves say "失敗之後要退回「連不上」，人類還可以再試一次" — retrying is the supported/expected UX, not a corner case.

3. Within one `run_declarative_rebind` call, the sequence is: read `human_disabled` (595) → `register_declarative_spec` (596, defaults every non-consent receptor to `enabled: !manifest.requires_consent`, confirmed at interaction-registry/src/lib.rs:128) → reapply disable via `set_receptor_enabled(false)` for each id in `human_disabled` (599-605) → unconditionally `clear_declarative_human_disabled` (608) → *then* wait up to 20s for the handshake (612-639), which can fail with `RebindStop::Failed` while the clear has already happened.

4. On that failure, `settle_declarative_rebind(.., false)` only flips the lifecycle to `Unbound{Disconnected}` (rebindable — confirmed `UnboundReason::Disconnected.rebindable() == true` at declarative_lifecycle.rs:79-81); it does not restore `human_disabled_receptors`. Nothing else in the runtime repopulates that field — grepping all uses confirms `note_declarative_human_disabled` is the sole writer and its only caller is the disable-transition branch.

5. So a second `transition_provider(Available)` call runs `run_declarative_rebind` again from scratch: it unregisters the receptor (still disabled from step 3 of the previous attempt) and re-registers it via the spec with the manifest default (enabled, since it doesn't require consent), and this time `human_disabled` is `[]`, so nothing re-disables it. The receptor ends up enabled — a capability the human explicitly turned off gets silently turned back on by a background/administrative retry the human only asked to "try connecting again," not "turn my sensor back on."

6. This is new code entirely introduced on this branch (`git log f5b8e2f..HEAD -- declarative_lifecycle.rs providers.rs` shows only `b32ba10 feat(runtime): rebind declarative devices without a restart...` and `9799b1e`), so it's in-scope. The only existing test for this bookkeeping, `rebind_keeps_human_disabled_receptors_off` (declarative_session_loop.rs:1950), covers only the single successful-handshake path and does not combine it with a prior failed handshake + retry, so the gap is real and untested.

This directly contradicts the guarantee the code's own comments state ("既有保證：回到 Available 不自動恢復任何能力", declarative_lifecycle.rs:593) and the repo's CLAUDE.md invariant that disabled capabilities must not auto-restore. It's scoped to non-consent-required receptors a human manually toggled off (not consent-gated sensors, which default closed regardless, and not actuators, which aren't tracked by this mechanism at all) — "high" rather than "blocker" is the right severity, matching the original report.

confirmed.fix: 把 `human_disabled_receptors` 當成「這台裝置目前應該保持關閉的受器」的持久事實，而不是一次性 token：只有在 rebind 真的收斂成 `Bound`（第 8 步）之後才清，或乾脆不清、改成每次停用時重新取樣＋每次 register 後一律套用。另可在 `transition_provider` 的非停用分支也先取樣一次（`receptor_flags == Some((false,true))`），讓任何觸發 rebind 的入口都帶著最新名單。
confirmed.regressionTest: Extend the pattern of `rebind_timeout_is_bounded_and_honest` with a non-consent receptor: build a dead_spec-like spec (unreachable serial port so handshake never completes) that also declares an 'ambient' receptor with no requiresConsent (default enabled=true); register it, then call rt.registry.set_receptor_enabled(&ambient_id,false) to simulate the human turning it off; transition_provider(Disabled) then transition_provider(Available) to start rebind attempt #1; wait_until a 'provider.rebind-failed' audit row appears (attempt #1 times out against the dead port) and assert the receptor is still disabled; call transition_provider(Available) again to start attempt #2; poll every ~200ms for a few seconds (well inside the 20s handshake budget) and assert the receptor stays disabled. The bug manifests as that assertion failing shortly after attempt #2 starts, because register_declarative_spec resets the receptor to enabled once human_disabled was cleared at the end of attempt #1. / Extend `declarative_session_loop.rs` with a test that: (1) uses the `rebind_keeps_human_disabled_receptors_off` setup (spec with a non-consent `ambient` receptor, join session, human calls `set_receptor_enabled(ambient_id, false)`); (2) disables the provider (`transition_provider(Disabled)`) so `note_declarative_human_disabled` records `ambient_id`; (3) forces the *first* re-enable's rebind to fail its handshake — e.g. by pointing `fx`'s port at a path with no responder for that attempt, or by injecting a fault so `channels.iter().all(|c| c.handshake_ready())` never becomes true within `REBIND_HANDSHAKE_BUDGET` — and waits for `provider.rebind-failed`/`Disconnected`; (4) then calls `transition_provider(Available)` again with the real fixture responding normally and waits for `Available`; (5) asserts `rt.registry.receptor(&ambient_id).await.is_err()` still holds after the *second, successful* rebind. Today this assertion fails: the receptor comes back enabled because `human_disabled_receptors` was cleared after step 3's registration succeeded, before its handshake timed out. Fix direction: only clear the record once `settle_declarative_rebind(.., true)` actually commits the rebind as successful (e.g. move the clear to after the handshake loop / step 8), while keeping today's rationale (clear before a stale list can hit a later *disconnect-triggered* rebind) — e.g. clear on both the success path and immediately when returning `RebindStop::Failed` from the handshake block is wrong; clear should happen only alongside `settle_declarative_rebind(provider_id, generation, true)`.

confirmed.title: 併發的 send_aip 會把兩則 envelope 的分片交錯寫上線，兩則都在對端整筆丟棄，而 host 兩次都回 Ok、沒有任何稽核
confirmed.file: crates/interaction-adapter-declarative/src/protocol.rs:779 (the `for (i, frame) in frames.iter().enumerate() { self.raw.send_before(...).await?... }` loop inside `DeviceLink::send_aip`) — line citation is accurate against the current file content.
confirmed.claim: `DeviceLink::send_aip` 把一則 envelope 切成 N 片後，用 N 次獨立的 `self.raw.send_before(...).await` 依序送出，中間**沒有任何 per-link 出站鎖**。同一條 link 上兩個併發的 `send_aip`（兩次 `character_session_apply`）會在 await 點交錯成 A0 B0 A1 B1…；重組器（host 端 `Reassembler` 與 `scripts/esp32-serial-sim.py` 的 `handle_aip_frag` 用同一套規則）看到 xfer 換掉就 supersede，之後的 seq!=0 一律 `unknown-xfer` → **兩則都完全丟失**。而每一片的 `send_before` 都成功，所以 `send_aip` 對兩則都回 `Ok`，`character_session_send` 不會寫 `aip.outbound-undeliverable`，host 端一行痕跡都沒有。這正是「已寫上線」被當成「送到了」的那一格。
confirmed.evidence: protocol.rs:736-790 `send_aip`：`let xfer = self.outbound_xfer.fetch_add(1, ...)`（773）後 `for (i, frame) in frames.iter().enumerate() { self.raw.send_before(encode_host_msg(frame), deadline).await?... }`（779-790）——沒有 mutex、每片一個 await。fragment.rs:299-315 `Reassembler::accept`：`if current.xfer != *xfer || current.generation != generation { superseded = self.cancel("superseded") }`；fragment.rs:337-341：`if self.current.is_none() { if seq != 0 { return refuse("unknown-xfer", 0) } }`。併發是既有事實而非假設：character_session.rs:2207 的註解自己寫著「`Output::Persist` 由各自的 `character_session_apply` **併發派送**」，而 `character_session_apply`(1924) 只在 `for output` 內序列化，`CharacterSessionHost::session()`(780) 的 std::Mutex 不跨 apply 持有。實測（scratchpad 小程式，直接呼叫本 crate 的 `fragment_envelope_line` + `Reassembler::accept`，limit=639）：A 切 2 片、B 切 2 片，交錯餵入後輸出 `frame (0,A)->buffered / frame (0,B)->superseded then buffered / frame (1,A)->superseded then unknown-xfer / frame (1,B)->dropped:unknown-xfer`，`completed envelopes = 0`。模擬器端規則相同（esp32-serial-sim.py `handle_aip_frag`：`if rx is not None and rx["xfer"] != xfer: drop_aip_rx("superseded")`、`if seq != 0: unknown-xfer`）。`tests/aip_link.rs`／`aip_fragment.rs` 共 31 測都是單一傳輸，沒有一支涵蓋併發送出。

verdicts.reasoning:
Verified end-to-end by direct code reading (no repo files modified).

1. New code, no prior atomicity to regress from: `git diff f5b8e2f..HEAD -- protocol.rs` shows the multi-frame branch of `send_aip` (fragment.rs entirely new, +443 lines) is 100% new in this branch. The pre-branch `send_aip` (git show f5b8e2f:...) always did exactly one `self.raw.send_before(...)` call — a single enqueue, no interleaving surface existed at all. This branch is what introduces the race.

2. No lock spans the multi-frame loop: read protocol.rs:773-791 directly — `xfer = self.outbound_xfer.fetch_add(...)` then `for (i, frame) in frames.iter().enumerate() { self.raw.send_before(encode_host_msg(frame), deadline).await?... }`. No mutex/semaphore wraps this loop, and grepped the whole adapter/runtime tree for any per-link or per-device outbound serialization (`tokio::sync::Mutex` near DeviceLink/DeviceOutbound/AipChannel/device_outbound) — none exists. `device_outbound()` (character_session.rs:950) just clones an `Arc<dyn DeviceOutbound>` out of an `RwLock` map; nothing guards concurrent calls into `send_aip` on the same channel.

3. Enqueue is per-frame, not per-transfer: `send_before` → `self.enqueue(line, deadline)` → `self.tx_out.try_send((line, deadline))` (serial.rs:402, and equivalent mpsc-style paths for mqtt/ble) — each frame is pushed to the outbound queue as an independent, individually-atomic operation. Two concurrent `send_aip` calls on the same link can legally interleave their `try_send` calls at frame granularity, and the single supervisor thread drains/writes them FIFO in that interleaved order.

4. Reassembly design guarantees total loss on interleaving: read `Reassembler::accept`/`accept_inner` (fragment.rs:281-370) directly — one in-flight transfer per link; a frame with a different `xfer` immediately supersedes (drops) the current one; and when there is no current transfer, any frame with `seq != 0` is refused as `unknown-xfer`. Tracing A0 B0 A1 B1 through this logic by hand: A0→buffered; B0→A superseded+dropped, B buffered; A1→B superseded+dropped, then A1 (seq=1, no current)→unknown-xfer, dropped; B1→(no current)→unknown-xfer, dropped. Both envelopes end up fully lost — matches the finding's claim exactly. Independently confirmed the **device-side** mirror of this same logic exists in `scripts/esp32-serial-sim.py::handle_aip_frag` (added in this same diff), which implements identical single-current-transfer/superseded/unknown-xfer semantics for frames arriving from the host — so it's not merely the host's inbound reassembler (used for DeviceMsg from the device) that's at stake; the actual attack surface (device receiving fragmented HostMsg::Aip) has the same drop behavior, confirmed via the simulator that stands in for firmware.

5. Silent success, no audit: `send_before`/`enqueue` return `Ok` on a successful `try_send`; nothing about queuing order or downstream drop reaches the caller. `send_aip` therefore returns `Ok(())` for both concurrent callers. `character_session_send` (character_session.rs:1952-1990) only emits the `aip.outbound-undeliverable` audit on an `Err` from `channel.send_aip(envelope).await` — with both calls returning Ok, no audit line is ever produced for this loss.

6. Concurrency is real and reachable, not hypothetical: multiple public entry points (`character_session_join`, `_leave`, `_presence`, `_submit` — all `.await character_session_apply(...)` inline in their own async call — plus `character_session_submit_runtime` via `character_session_dispatch_later`, which `tokio::spawn`s a detached task) can each independently produce `Output::Send`/`Output::Broadcast` to the same device concurrently with no serialization across calls. The code's own test comment (character_session.rs ~2207) explicitly documents this as known/expected: "`Output::Persist` 由各自的 `character_session_apply` 併發派送" — the persist path was hardened against exactly this concurrency (stale-revision guard), but the `send_aip` path was not. The fragment.rs module comment itself names the two message shapes that require fragmentation — the initial `state{kind:"snapshot"}` reply and any patch carrying `members` — and a `members`-patch broadcast is precisely what fires to all already-online devices whenever another device joins/leaves, so two near-simultaneous device joins/leaves plausibly produce two concurrent oversized broadcasts to the same third device on the same link.

7. No test coverage: grepped both `tests/aip_link.rs` (14 tests) and `tests/aip_fragment.rs` (17 tests) — all exercise a single transfer in isolation; none use `tokio::join!`/`spawn` to drive two concurrent `send_aip`/fragment transfers on one link.

Net: the mechanism, the reachability, and the "no audit despite two lost envelopes" consequence are all independently verified against the actual current file contents, not just the write-up's assertions. I could not find any mitigating serialization I might have missed, and the file/line citation is exact.

One nuance worth surfacing (does not change the verdict): the protocol does have an `aip-resume` mechanism (character_session.rs:1274) for revision-gap recovery, which could eventually paper over a lost broadcast if the device proactively detects a revision gap and asks to resume — but that is a separate, best-effort self-healing path, not an audit trail, and does not contradict the finding's core claim that the loss itself is silent and misreported as `Ok` at the point it happens.

I tried hard to refute this and could not — every load-bearing claim checks out against the current code, and I independently reproduced the failure with fresh code rather than trusting the reporter's numbers.

1. Mechanism in `DeviceLink::send_aip` (protocol.rs:736-793): the fragmentation branch is brand-new in this diff (confirmed via `git diff f5b8e2f..HEAD -- protocol.rs`: `fragment_envelope_line`/`Reassembler` import, `outbound_xfer` field, and the whole fragmenting branch are additions, not pre-existing code). It allocates `xfer` via an atomic (773), then loops `for (i, frame) in frames.iter().enumerate() { self.raw.send_before(...).await?... }` (779-790) with no lock held across the loop. I checked every layer between this and its callers (`ensure_ready_generation`'s `tokio::sync::Mutex<handshaken>` is dropped before the loop runs; `AipChannel::send_aip` at protocol.rs:1576 just forwards; `DeclarativeOutbound::send_aip` in declarative_session.rs just forwards; `device_outbound()` in character_session.rs:950 returns a cloned `Arc` to the same shared channel/link for a given device id) — there is no synchronization anywhere serializing two concurrent multi-frame sends to the same device.

2. Concurrency is real, not hypothetical: `character_session.rs:2207`'s own test comment states "`Output::Persist` 由各自的 `character_session_apply` 併發派送" — and the code confirms it: `character_session_device_frame` is invoked from independent per-device receive-loop tasks (declarative_session.rs:319, mobile.rs:3805), and `interaction-cli/src/main.rs:308` builds a `new_multi_thread` tokio runtime, so two such tasks can run in true OS-thread parallel, not just cooperatively interleaved. The project's own progress doc (`docs/releases/v0.6.x-maintainability-progress.md:63`) documents this exact "apply() runs concurrently" hazard and shows it was fixed for `Output::Persist` (epoch/revision guard) but says nothing about the outbound-send/fragmentation path — so this is a real, unaddressed gap in the same known hazard class, not a documented/accepted limitation.

3. Fragmentation is easily reachable, not a corner case: Serial and MQTT both cap lines at ~639 bytes and BLE at a small write size (protocol.rs comments, mqtt.rs:294, ble.rs:507) — ordinary AIP envelopes (session state, capability payloads) can exceed that routinely.

4. I independently reproduced the reassembly-side catastrophe with my own throwaway program (not reusing the reporter's script), calling the real `fragment_envelope_line` + `Reassembler::accept` from a separate scratch crate path-depending on `interaction-adapter-declarative`: feeding A0,B0,A1,B1 (two real 3-fragment transfers) yields `Buffered → Superseded(drop A,"superseded") → Superseded(drop B,"superseded")+Dropped(A,"unknown-xfer") → Dropped(B,"unknown-xfer")`, ending with `has_transfer()==false` — i.e. both envelopes are completely and silently lost, exactly as claimed.

5. I confirmed `scripts/esp32-serial-sim.py:799-846 handle_aip_frag` implements the identical supersede/unknown-xfer algorithm (its own comment says "規則與 host 的 Reassembler 相同"), supporting the claim that a real device-side reassembler would behave the same way.

6. I confirmed the "no audit" claim: `character_session_send` (character_session.rs:1955) only emits `aip.outbound-undeliverable` when `channel.send_aip(...)` returns `Err`; since every individual `send_before` call for each fragment succeeds (it's genuinely written to the wire), `send_aip` returns `Ok` for both concurrent callers, so no audit event fires for either lost envelope.

7. I checked the 31 existing tests in `tests/aip_link.rs` and `tests/aip_fragment.rs`: none use `tokio::spawn`/`join!`/concurrent sends, and the closest test (`a_new_transfer_cancels_the_previous_one_and_says_so`) only feeds `first[0]` then `second[0]` — it never continues feeding `first[1]` afterward, so it never exercises the "second fragment of the pre-empted transfer becomes an orphaned unknown-xfer, losing the new transfer too" tail that this finding hinges on. This is a genuine, real, unmitigated concurrency bug in newly-added code, matching the file/line/severity as reported.

confirmed.fix: 在 `DeviceLink` 加一把出站序列化鎖（`tokio::sync::Mutex<()>`），`send_aip` 只在需要分片時（或一律）整段 N 片持鎖送完再放；或改由單一 writer task 以「整筆傳輸」為單位排隊。無論哪種，都要保證一筆 xfer 的所有片在線上連續。順帶：若中途放棄，應對呼叫端回 Err 並留 `aip.outbound-undeliverable`，不要讓「片送出去了但整則沒到」變成 Ok。
confirmed.regressionTest: In `crates/interaction-adapter-declarative/tests/aip_fragment.rs` (or a new `aip_link_concurrency.rs`), build two envelopes each large enough to require ≥2 frames at the test link's line limit, and drive them through a fake `RawLink` whose `send_before` is instrumented to yield at each call (e.g. `tokio::task::yield_now().await` before enqueueing) so the scheduler is likely to interleave. Spawn two tasks calling `link.send_aip(&envelope_a, ...)` and `link.send_aip(&envelope_b, ...)` concurrently via `tokio::join!`, capture the exact sequence of lines the fake link received, feed that sequence into `Reassembler::accept` in order, and assert that at least one of the two envelopes reaches `ReassemblyStep::Completed`. Today's code will interleave A0 B0 A1 B1 and both assertions of "at least one envelope completed" and "no unaudited loss" will fail — proving the race — until `send_aip`'s per-transfer frame loop is protected by a per-link outbound lock (e.g. `tokio::sync::Mutex` held for the whole fragmentation loop, or a per-link `mpsc` actor that serializes whole envelopes rather than individual lines). / In interaction-adapter-declarative (or a runtime-level integration test): spin up a mock RawLink with a small max_line_bytes and frag capability advertised; wrap the DeviceLink in an Arc; spawn two tokio tasks that concurrently call `link.send_aip(&envelope_a, timeout)` and `link.send_aip(&envelope_b, timeout)` where both envelopes exceed max_line_bytes (need >=2 fragments each); on the "device" side, feed every line the mock transport captured, in the order actually written, into a `Reassembler` (or the python simulator's handle_aip_frag semantics) and assert that at least one of the two envelopes reassembles successfully. Today this can flake/fail because interleaving loses both, while every character_session_send caller currently sees Ok for both `send_aip` calls with zero audit trail. Fix direction: serialize each link's whole multi-frame `send_aip` sequence under a per-link async mutex (or hand the whole envelope's frames to a single writer task/queue) so two concurrent transfers to the same device never interleave on the wire.

verdicts.reasoning:
Verified against the current file contents (this branch's new commits 9799b1e / bc6d834, not pre-existing code — `git log f5b8e2f..HEAD` shows these files' diffs are entirely new to this branch).

1. `derive_sync_profile` at character_session.rs:193-194 is exactly as quoted: `carries_snapshot = channel.max_line_bytes().is_none() || channel.supports_fragmentation()`; `true` → `SYNC_PROFILE_FULL_STATE`.
2. `DeviceLink::supports_fragmentation()` (protocol.rs:719-721) is literally `self.advertises(FRAG_CAP) == Some(true)`, and `advertises()` (protocol.rs:824-830) reads `advertised_caps`, populated only by `store_caps(caps)` (protocol.rs:999) from the device's `hello.caps` field. The handshake code's own comment right above it says in Chinese: "hello.caps 是裝置自報的能力清單" (hello.caps is the device's self-reported capability list) — the implementation itself labels this exact value as self-reported, which is the opposite of what device-profile.md §3.1 claims ("裝置不該（也不能）自己宣稱『我拿得到完整狀態』… 不是它的意見").
3. There is zero verification path: `accept_fragment` only checks the *inbound* direction (rejects fragments arriving from a device that never advertised `FRAG_CAP`); there is no ack, no round-trip proof, no "reassembly succeeded" signal from device to host anywhere in the protocol (character-session.md §restricts member message types to event/cancel/query/result/heartbeat/capability — no state-ack type exists by design). `send_aip`'s own doc comment confirms the honesty ladder is already understood at the transport layer: "誠實階梯：Ok 只代表這一行已經寫上線…不代表裝置收到、更不代表它套用了" — yet that ladder is erased one layer up when `full-state`/"已同步" is derived from mere capability presence.
4. Timing makes it worse than the finding states: `audit_member_sync_profile` is invoked from the join path (character_session.rs:1131, inside `character_session_join`) *before* `character_session_apply(joined.outputs)` even attempts to send the very first join snapshot. So `full-state`/"已同步" is asserted before any real transfer — successful or not — has ever been attempted, and `derive_sync_profile` is never re-evaluated in light of later `aip.fragment-dropped`/`aip.outbound-undeliverable` failures (only two call sites exist: the join-time audit and the lazy diagnostics/status projection, both re-deriving from the same static, cached capability list). A device that falsely advertises `aip.frag/1` in `hello.caps` will show a permanent, never-corrected green "已同步" for the life of the connection even if every oversized envelope is silently dropped on its end.
5. UI consequence verified directly in characterSync.ts: `characterSyncProfileLabel` returns `null` for `full-state` (line ~263), so the `partial-sync` branch in `projectCharacterSession` (~line 636) never fires for such a member, and it falls through to `project("synced")` (~line 652) — the green "已同步" badge, exactly as claimed.
6. This is new in this branch, not a pre-existing/already-covered issue: the whole `derive_sync_profile`/fragmentation feature was added by commits 9799b1e and bc6d834 in this branch, and it is not mentioned anywhere in CHANGELOG.md's [Unreleased] section or docs/releases/v0.6.x-maintainability-progress.md (grepped, zero hits for "frag"/"syncProfile"/"derive_sync_profile"), so it is not recorded as a documented/accepted known limitation either — device-profile.md §6.3's "已知限制" only discusses the reference firmware's choice not to declare the cap (so it isn't affected), not the general risk that any device (especially given the already-weak `transport-hello+device-side-pairing` identity strength, which the docs admit lets "任何能開那個埠／topic 的程序" impersonate the device) can falsely claim it and get an unverifiable, permanent "已同步" status.

This is a genuine violation of the CLAUDE.md-mandated honesty ladder ("completed≠verified…不得謊稱成功") and directly contradicts the project's own docs (device-profile.md §3.1) about what "Runtime derives, not device's opinion" is supposed to mean. Severity high is appropriate: it's a persistent, uncorrectable false-positive in a status the UI presents to the human as ground truth, on a transport whose identity is already known-weak — but it does not bypass the Policy Governor or actual actuator safety limits (impact is confined to a misleading sync/status indicator, safety-critical text still routes through system.text/host overlay per the architecture), so it stays at high rather than blocker.

Traced the full chain in current code: derive_sync_profile (character_session.rs:193) returns full-state whenever channel.max_line_bytes().is_none() || channel.supports_fragmentation() — checked before role is even considered. DeviceLink::supports_fragmentation (protocol.rs:719-720) is literally self.advertises(FRAG_CAP)==Some(true), and advertises()/store_caps (protocol.rs:824-842, 999) read the value straight out of the device's own hello.caps with no ack, no reassembly-success receipt, and no independent corroboration — send_aip just streams fragment frames via raw.send_before with no per-fragment confirmation (protocol.rs's own doc comment: AIP replies are the peer sending back another envelope, not a wire-level ack). On the frontend, characterSyncProfileLabel (characterSync.ts:263) returns null for full-state, which is exactly what lets projectCharacterSession (line 636-654) and characterSyncDeviceLine (line 725) fall through to the "synced"/"角色同步：已同步" green-check outcome. device-profile.md §3.1 explicitly frames full-state as "那是那條線的事實，不是它的意見" and the one profile allowed to say "已同步", while §6.3 itself admits in prose that a firmware which (mis)declares aip.frag/1 without a real reassembly buffer would have every oversized snapshot silently dropped device-side while the host's own receipt says only "已送出" — i.e., the docs already know the self-declaration can be false and unverifiable, yet the syncProfile classification built in this branch treats it as sufficient for the strongest UI claim, with no equivalent of the identityStrength caveat ("介面不得把 transport-hello+device-side-pairing 顯示成已驗證身分") and no equivalent of the role-clamping/anti-spoofing precedent this same codebase already established for `degraded` (explicitly citing prior finding capability-consent-052/general-mode-ux-022 about not trusting self-reported role for UI conclusions). This is a genuine, newly introduced (commit 600f030, this branch) honesty-ladder gap, not a pre-existing/already-covered/style issue, and it is not recorded anywhere as a known limitation (grepped v0.6.x-maintainability-progress.md, CHANGELOG.md, acceptance-evidence.md — no hits for syncProfile/FRAG_CAP trust caveat).

confirmed.fix: 兩條路擇一：(a) 把 `full-state` 降格為「宣告的」，只有在**觀察到**對端真的收下一則分片傳輸（例如要求 `aip.frag/1` 的裝置對整筆傳輸回一則 ack／或以後續的 resume(lastRevision) 證明它收到了那個 revision）之後才升級，未證實前一律 `intent-only`，UI 不得綠勾；(b) 保留現行推導但把文件與 characterSync.ts:238 的註解改成事實（「這一半來自裝置的能力宣告，未經驗證」），並讓 UI 對「僅憑宣告」的 full-state 用不同於已同步的文案。

verdicts.reasoning:
Verified every link in the chain directly in the current code:

1. apps/interaction-desktop/src/pages/ConnectPage.tsx:546-552 — `id = String(identity.id ?? "")` where `identity` comes from `providers.data` (api.providersList(), i.e. GET /v1/providers → Rust `ProviderDescriptor`), then `syncProfiles[id]` is looked up.
2. crates/interaction-core/src/provider.rs:179-194 — `ProviderDescriptor` has fields `identity, state, receptors, actuators, tool_operations, paired_at, last_seen, detail` — no `deviceId` field of any kind, so `identity.id` (the provider id) is the only key ConnectPage has to look up with.
3. crates/interaction-runtime/src/providers.rs:743 — a declarative spec with no `provider:` block (the common/default path, and the only path this branch's own new example `examples/adapters/event-source-button.yaml` uses) gets `ProviderId::new(format!("provider.adapter.{}", spec.id))`, e.g. `provider.adapter.button-box`.
4. crates/interaction-runtime/src/declarative_session.rs:159-160 and character_session.rs:1008-1013 — the character-session `Party` for that same device is `Party::device(self.channel.expected_device_id())`, and `character_session_sync_profiles()` serializes `"deviceId": m.party.id` — i.e. the AIP `expectedDeviceId`, e.g. `button-box-01` in the same example file. This is structurally a different string (different prefix, different value) from the provider id, and there is no override path in the default registration flow that makes them equal.
5. apps/interaction-desktop/src/statusProjection/characterSync.ts:286-320 — `characterSyncProfiles()` keys its output map by exactly that `deviceId` field from `characterSessionSync[]` (or `party.id` from diagnostics `members[]`), confirming the dictionary key really is the AIP device id, not the provider id.
6. apps/interaction-desktop/src/test/connectPage.test.tsx:1157-1170 and 1370-1386 — `providerRow()` sets `identity.id = "provider.esp32.desk"`, and the guard test sets `characterSessionSync[].deviceId = "provider.esp32.desk"` too — i.e. the test manufactures a coincidental match between a provider-id-shaped string and a device-id field, a shape the real runtime never produces (real deviceId values come from `expectedDeviceId`, e.g. `button-box-01` / `esp32-sim01` per crates/interaction-runtime/tests/declarative_session_loop.rs:160-163, never from the provider-id template).

Net effect confirmed: for every declarative device provider registered through the documented default path (no explicit `provider:` override), `syncProfiles[id]` at ConnectPage.tsx:552 looks up the wrong key and always returns `undefined`, so `syncNote` is always `null` in production. The docs/aip/general-mode-ux.md §5.7 promise ("只回報事件：這台裝置收不到完整的角色狀態，不算已同步。" on the device-list entry) is unreachable for any real declarative device, while the only test covering this path (connectPage.test.tsx ~line 1368-1386) passes only because it fabricates matching provider-id-shaped strings on both sides — it does not exercise the actual production id mismatch and would not catch this bug. This also means the `open-devices` action from the character-sync card (which routes users to this exact Connect page section per general-mode-ux.md) lands them on a page that, for the affected device, silently shows no explanation at all.

Verified end-to-end against current file contents (no line drift):

1. ConnectPage.tsx:546/552 — `const id = String(identity.id ?? "")` then `characterSyncProfileNote(syncProfiles[id])`. `identity` comes from `deviceProviders` (`providers.data`, from `api.providersList()` → Tauri `providers_list` → `runtime.list_providers()` → `ProviderDescriptor.identity`, unmodified).

2. `characterSyncProfiles()` (apps/interaction-desktop/src/statusProjection/characterSync.ts:286-314) keys its returned map by `characterSessionSync[].deviceId` or `members[].party.id` where `party.kind === "device"`.

3. Runtime side: `character_session.rs:1012` sets `"deviceId": m.party.id`, and `declarative_session.rs:158-160` (`DeviceBinding::party`) builds that party as `Party::device(self.channel.expected_device_id())` — i.e., the AIP device id is always the human-authored `expectedDeviceId` field from the channel config (protocol.rs confirms `expected_device_id` is a required, independent field with no fallback to the spec id).

4. Provider id, by contrast, defaults (when no `provider:` block is given) to `provider.adapter.<spec.id>` (providers.rs:743, in `register_declarative_spec`) — a different string built from the spec's top-level `id`, not from `expectedDeviceId`.

5. The only shipped example, `examples/adapters/event-source-button.yaml`, confirms the two fields are independent and different in practice: `id: button-box` (→ provider id `provider.adapter.button-box`) vs `expectedDeviceId: button-box-01` (→ AIP device id). No `provider:` override block exists in this file, nor anywhere else in the repo (grepped `^provider:` in all yaml — no hits), so there is no shipped mechanism or documented pattern that would make these two strings coincide.

6. The runtime's own multi-instance test fixture (`declarative_session_loop.rs` `Fixture::spawn_with`) deliberately keeps them distinct: `provider_id = format!("provider.adapter.{spec_id}")` vs `device_id = format!("esp32-sim{seq:02}")`, with a comment explaining exactly why they must be different namespaces.

7. The frontend test at connectPage.test.tsx:1157-1170 (`providerRow`) hardcodes `identity.id: "provider.esp32.desk"`, and the test at line ~1373 sets `characterSessionSync[].deviceId: "provider.esp32.desk"` — the identical literal string. This string appears nowhere else in the repo as a real provider-id-generation convention (grep confirms zero other occurrences), so the test is manufacturing a coincidental match rather than reflecting how `providers_list`/`character_session_sync_profiles` actually produce these two ids in production. The test therefore passes while asserting nothing about the real key-space mismatch.

Net effect: for every declarative hardware device provider shipped/documented in this repo, `syncProfiles[id]` at ConnectPage.tsx:552 looks up the wrong key and returns `undefined`, so `characterSyncProfileNote` returns `null` and the promised `docs/aip/general-mode-ux.md` §5.7 partial-sync disclosure ("這台裝置收不到完整的角色狀態，不算已同步。") can never render on the connect/devices list for a real button-box-style adapter — even though the phone-card path two dozen lines above (line 530-533, using `m.deviceId`) does it correctly, showing the bug is an id-namespace mix-up specific to the declarative-provider list item, not a stylistic choice or something covered by another mechanism. This is a genuine general-mode-ux / honesty-ladder gap: a documented safety/honesty disclosure is silently dead code in production, and the accompanying test is self-validating rather than proving the real behavior.

No part of the finding was refuted; every file/line/test reference checked out exactly as stated, and the two flagged CHANGELOG bullets are demonstrably false given code shipped in this very branch range. This is a genuine, reproducible self-contract violation (the section's own header promises deletion-on-fix; CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md also mandate syncing known-limitations on fix) with concrete evidence of misleading documentation, not a style nitpick or already-fixed report.

Every load-bearing claim in the finding checks out, and I could not construct a valid rebuttal.

1. Zero-diff proof: `git show f5b8e2f:CHANGELOG.md` is byte-identical to the working-tree CHANGELOG.md (`diff` produces no output). 29 commits (not 28 — minor count error in the finding, 9 of them `feat`) landed with not a single CHANGELOG.md edit. docs/acceptance-evidence.md and docs/releases/evidence-index.json are likewise absent from `git diff --name-only f5b8e2f..HEAD`.

4. Cross-contamination: docs/acceptance-evidence.md:944 (also untouched this branch) repeats the same now-superseded 639-byte claim without qualification, so the staleness isn't confined to one file — it's a synchronization failure across the doc set that CLAUDE.md:79 and AGENTS.md:96 explicitly require kept in sync ("已知限制記錄在 CHANGELOG.md 與 docs/acceptance-evidence.md，修掉時同步更新").

Process check: `scripts/release-prepare.sh` (lines 42-64) hard-fails ("write the release notes before preparing") if `[Unreleased]` is empty at release time and otherwise renames it verbatim — it does not auto-generate entries. 7. Scope compliance: CHANGELOG.md/acceptance-evidence.md themselves are unchanged files, but per the review's own scoping rule ("舊碼未動的部分只在「本分支的變更讓它變錯」時才報"), this is exactly the case where the branch's own code changes (fragmentation, restart-free rebind) made pre-existing doc claims false — squarely in-scope.

The only inaccuracies I found in the finding are cosmetic (commit count 29 vs claimed 28, feat-commit count 9 vs claimed 8), which don't affect the substance.
