confirmed.claim: 文件開頭寫「五個演練各自真的做了一次（不是紙上推演），每一個都有自己的 commit」，並在 :11 規定「文件裡一律用檔案路徑引用，不引用本分支的 commit」。實際上演練 1（`ref-dot`）與演練 3（`SemanticState.ambient`）的 commit 只存在於本機 worktree 分支 `wt/drills`，不是 `feature/v0.6.x-maintainability` 的祖先，也沒有推到 origin；它們引用的檔案在 HEAD 上一個都不存在。於是 §1／§3 的頭條數字（vitest 1759/1759、`interaction-session` 139/139）在本分支（以及任何 reviewer／CI 拿得到的 ref 上）無法重現、無法稽核，而文件的引用規則又保證讀者拿不到能找到它們的 commit id。§7 F1／F2 的「重現：`git show` 演練 1 的 commit」同樣無法執行。
confirmed.evidence: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 89ac7af HEAD` → NOT ancestor；`git branch -a --contains 89ac7af` → 只有 `wt/drills`（同理 bc3dc73＝演練 3）。`git ls-remote --heads origin` 只有 feature/v0.6.0-foundation、feature/v0.6.x-maintainability、main、release/v0.5.0-*、release/v0.5.1-*，沒有 wt/drills。HEAD 上 `ls apps/interaction-desktop/public/characters/` 沒有 `ref-dot`；`rg -l 'ref-dot' .` 只命中這份文件本身；`rg -n SHIPPED_CHARACTER_IDS apps/interaction-desktop/src/test/character-manifests.test.ts` 無命中；`crates/interaction-session/tests/` 沒有 `optional_state_field.rs`。另外 :9「**這個分支不會合併**」在這份文件所在的分支上讀起來是錯的——文件本身、`examples/adapters/event-source-button.yaml`、`scripts/drills/*.sh`、演練 2 的測試都已經在 feature/v0.6.x-maintainability 上。

verdicts.reasoning:
Verified every factual claim independently on the actual current HEAD (2aad4dd, on branch feature/v0.6.x-maintainability):

1. docs/releases/v0.7.0-drills.md exists on HEAD with the exact quoted text at the exact line numbers: :5 "每一個都有自己的 commit", :9 "這個分支不會合併", :11 "文件裡一律用檔案路徑引用，不引用本分支的 commit。"

2. Commit ancestry: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 89ac7af HEAD` → not an ancestor; `git merge-base --is-ancestor bc3dc73 HEAD` → not an ancestor. These are drill 1 (`drill(character): add a third reference character`) and drill 3 (`drill(session): add one optional SemanticState field`) from the `wt/drills` branch (backing worktree `/Users/user/Workspace/claude-lab/ai-wt-swift`), which is a purely local branch/worktree — `git ls-remote --heads origin` lists no `wt/drills`, only `feature/v0.6.x-maintainability` at `f5b8e2f` (the review's own diff base) and other known branches.

3. By contrast, drills 2, 4, 5 (device/lifecycle/storage) *were* brought onto this branch as commits d391f38/3b0af66/75a6f27, and the doc commit itself (713f8fe, content-identical to wt/drills' a7a3434) is on this branch — confirming the branch selectively carried over 3 of 5 drill commits but not all 5, while the doc still claims all 5 have commits.

4. Filesystem confirms drills 1/3 artifacts are absent from HEAD: `apps/interaction-desktop/public/characters/ref-dot/` missing, `character-ref-dot.test.ts` missing, repo-wide `rg -l "ref-dot"` matches only the doc file itself; `crates/interaction-session/tests/` has no `optional_state_field.rs` and no `ambient` field anywhere in `interaction-session/src`.

5. §7 F1's "重現：`git show` 演練 1 的 commit" is indeed unexecutable for anyone without access to the reviewer's specific local `wt/drills` branch/worktree — the object is reachable only there, not from any ref a fresh clone or CI checkout of origin would have.

6. :9's "這個分支不會合併" is verifiably false as a description of the branch this doc lives on: `examples/adapters/event-source-button.yaml` and `scripts/drills/*.sh` (referenced as reusable artifacts) are already committed on `feature/v0.6.x-maintainability` alongside the doc itself.

7. Checked for "already fixed" possibility: a later commit 2aad4dd (after 713f8fe, the run's labeled base) did land on this branch and fixed one of the *sub*-issues the drills doc's own §7 F2 flagged (consolidating `SHIPPED_CHARACTER_IDS` in `character-manifests.test.ts`), but `git diff 713f8fe HEAD -- docs/releases/v0.7.0-drills.md` is empty — the doc's text, including the exact lines under review, is byte-identical at current HEAD. So the finding is not stale/already-fixed; it fully survives at today's HEAD (2aad4dd), just with the file-line anchor unchanged.

No exculpatory reading survives: the claim "each of the five drills has its own commit" is false for 2 of 5 as measured against any ref reachable from origin or from this branch, and the doc's own citation rule (path-only, no commit ids) is precisely what prevents a reader from discovering this on their own.

confirmed.fix: 在 §1／§3 標題下明寫「證據 commit 在未合併的 `wt/drills`（89ac7af／bc3dc73），本分支上不可重現」，或把兩個 commit 也推到 origin 並破例寫出 sha；並把 :9 的「這個分支不會合併」改成指名 `wt/drills`，避免在本分支上自我否定。
confirmed.regressionTest: A doc-integrity check script could assert: for every commit hash mentioned as backing a claim in docs/releases/*.md (if any survive review as needing commit refs), `git merge-base --is-ancestor <hash> HEAD` must succeed; more directly here, add a CI/lint step (or a manual release-verify.sh check) that greps release/drill docs for characteristic artifact paths they claim to have exercised (e.g. `public/characters/ref-dot`, `crates/interaction-session/tests/optional_state_field.rs`) and fails if those paths don't exist on the branch being verified — catching exactly this "doc claims artifact X was built and tested" vs. "artifact X is absent from the tree" mismatch.

confirmed.title: 同一輪文件對同一批測試檔給出互相矛盾的計數（device-profile §6：13／6 vs §6.3 與 transport-bindings：26／14／24／17）
confirmed.file: docs/aip/device-profile.md:133-136 (contradicts its own :283-285 and docs/aip/transport-bindings.md:310-313; docs/acceptance-evidence.md:944 carries the same stale numbers)
confirmed.claim: `device-profile.md:133-136` 的「證據等級」仍寫 `declarative_session_loop.rs`（13 測）、`aip_link.rs` 6 測，而同一份文件 §6.3（:275-277）寫 `aip_fragment.rs` 17 測、`aip_link.rs` 14 測，`transport-bindings.md:310-313` 寫 `declarative_session_loop.rs` 25 測、`aip_link.rs` 14、`esp32_sim_conformance.rs` 24。三個數字彼此矛盾，而且沒有一個等於 HEAD 的實際值。`docs/acceptance-evidence.md:944` 也還停在 13／6。CLAUDE.md／AGENTS.md 要求「交付前回報**實際數字**」，這些是文件對外的證據強度宣稱，讀者無法判斷哪一個是真的。
confirmed.evidence: HEAD 實際計數（`grep -c '#\[tokio::test\|#\[test\]'`）：`crates/interaction-runtime/tests/declarative_session_loop.rs` = 26（列舉測試函式亦為 26：325…2091）、`crates/interaction-adapter-declarative/tests/aip_link.rs` = 14、`tests/esp32_sim_conformance.rs` = 24、`tests/aip_fragment.rs` = 17。transport-bindings.md:310 的 25 少算了 d391f38 新增的 `an_event_only_device_is_an_event_source_member`（declarative_session_loop.rs:2091）。

verdicts.reasoning:
Independently reproduced every number in the finding.

Actual HEAD test counts (via `grep -cE '^\s*#\[(tokio::)?test'`, cross-checked against listed `#[tokio::test(...)]` lines):
- crates/interaction-runtime/tests/declarative_session_loop.rs = 26 (attributes at lines 324…2091, last one being `an_event_only_device_is_an_event_source_member` at line 2091)
- crates/interaction-adapter-declarative/tests/aip_link.rs = 14
- crates/interaction-adapter-declarative/tests/esp32_sim_conformance.rs = 24
- crates/interaction-adapter-declarative/tests/aip_fragment.rs = 17

Documented numbers, confirmed at the exact cited lines:
- docs/aip/device-profile.md:133-136 (§6, "證據等級"): declarative_session_loop.rs "13 測", aip_link.rs "6 測", esp32_sim_conformance.rs "三方一致 2 測"
- docs/aip/device-profile.md:283-285 (§6.3, "證據等級"): aip_fragment.rs "17 測", aip_link.rs "14 測"
- docs/aip/transport-bindings.md:310-313 ("證據"): declarative_session_loop.rs "25 測", aip_fragment.rs "17 測", aip_link.rs "14 測", esp32_sim_conformance.rs "24 測"
- docs/acceptance-evidence.md:944: declarative_session_loop.rs "13 測", aip_link.rs "6", esp32_sim_conformance.rs "三方一致 2"

`git blame` confirms the drift mechanism exactly as the finding describes: device-profile.md §6 (lines 133-137) and acceptance-evidence.md:944 were both written on 2026-09-05 (commits fb097d47/e3050ec0 and 600f030b) before the v1.2 fragmentation feature landed. Commit 9799b1ea (2026-09-06 01:20-01:38) added aip_fragment.rs and rewrote aip_link.rs (6→14 tests) and declarative_session_loop.rs's evidence count to "25", authoring device-profile.md §6.3 and transport-bindings.md:310-313 — but never touched §6's now-stale "6 測"/"13 測" bullet, so the same document (device-profile.md) now asserts two different aip_link.rs counts (6 vs 14) for the same file. Then commit d391f38 (2026-09-06 02:15:58, after 9799b1ea) added a 26th test (`an_event_only_device_is_an_event_source_member`) to declarative_session_loop.rs, which postdates and invalidates transport-bindings.md's "25 測" — confirmed by `git log -S` showing d391f38 is the sole commit introducing that function. The branch's final commit 2aad4dd (02:31:02) touched device-profile.md again (adding an unrelated `Bound` clarification) without correcting any of these counts, so the contradiction ships to HEAD unresolved.

So: three genuinely different, mutually contradictory numbers exist for declarative_session_loop.rs (13 / 25 / 26-actual) and two for aip_link.rs (6 / 14, actual 14) across the cited documents, with none of the "13/6/2" trio matching HEAD and the "25" also now short by one. This is a real, verifiable evidence-accounting defect (documentation drift), not a resolved or misread issue — the file:line citations in the finding are accurate and the arithmetic checks out.

confirmed.fix: 把 device-profile.md:133 與 acceptance-evidence.md:944 的 13／6 更新為 26／14（並說明其中哪幾支屬於 D1／D2／分片／rebind），transport-bindings.md:310 的 25→26；或改成不寫絕對數字、只引用測試名，讓 `scripts/tests/architecture-checks.sh` 的清單成為唯一計數來源。
confirmed.regressionTest: Add a docs-claims.sh check (the repo already has this lint pattern for the deprecation ledger, per commit 2aad4dd) that greps each `tests/*.rs` file's `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]` count and cross-checks it against every "`<filename>` N 測" occurrence across docs/aip/*.md and docs/acceptance-evidence.md, failing CI when any two citations of the same file disagree with each other or with the live count.

confirmed.title: AGENTS.md §7 的「接續進度」指向不存在的章節與不存在的檔案，而它指的 progress 文件停在上一輪
confirmed.file: AGENTS.md:101-104
confirmed.claim: 本分支用一份獨立檔案取代了原本指向 CLAUDE.md 的 AGENTS.md symlink，新的 §7 規定「新 session 先讀進度文件的 §4（Blockers）與 §5，再決定動什麼」，並指向 (a)`docs/releases/v0.6.x-maintainability-progress.md`、(b)`docs/releases/v0.7.0-progress.md`（「若檔案還不在，以上一份為準」）。(b) 不存在；(a) 只有 §0–§4，**沒有 §5**；而且 (a) 完全沒有被本輪 28 個 commit 更新——它結尾寫「本輪已收尾」「已完成：M1 全部、M2 §3.1–§3.5、M3 §4.1–§4.4、M4 §5.1／§5.2／§5.3」，本輪落地的裝置線 v1.2 分片、免重啟 rebind 生命週期、三端接收端決策表、未解決停止、MAINTAINERS-MAP、deprecation-ledger、architecture-checks、五個演練一項都沒有。照 AGENTS.md 走的新 session 會得到「上一輪已收尾、沒有新東西」的結論——正是這份 progress 文件開頭宣稱要避免的失敗（「讓任何新的 session 能從檔案恢復，而不依賴聊天上下文」）。
confirmed.evidence: `grep -n '^## ' docs/releases/v0.6.x-maintainability-progress.md` → 只有 `## 0.`／`## 1.`／`## 2.`／`## 3.`／`## 4. Blockers（需要人）`，檔案於 `## 4.` 之後結束。`ls docs/releases/v0.7.0-progress.md` → No such file or directory。`git diff --name-only f5b8e2f..HEAD` 不含 v0.6.x-maintainability-progress.md。AGENTS.md 由 symlink→standalone 的改動見 commit 160d880／248e120。

verdicts.reasoning:
Every factual claim in the finding checks out against the live repo:

1. AGENTS.md:99-104 (§7 "接續進度") does say to read the progress file's §4 (Blockers) and §5, then names (a) docs/releases/v0.6.x-maintainability-progress.md and (b) docs/releases/v0.7.0-progress.md with "若檔案還不在，以上一份為準" — verified verbatim, line 104 matches exactly.

2. `grep -n '^## ' docs/releases/v0.6.x-maintainability-progress.md` returns only §0–§4 (ends at "## 4. Blockers（需要人）", line 182, file is 187 lines total). There is no §5. Confirmed.

3. `docs/releases/v0.7.0-progress.md` does not exist on this branch (`ls` → No such file or directory) and is not part of this branch's diff (`git diff --name-only f5b8e2f..HEAD` doesn't touch it). Confirmed.

4. The progress file was not touched anywhere in this branch's diff (`git diff --stat f5b8e2f..HEAD -- docs/releases/v0.6.x-maintainability-progress.md` is empty), yet 29 commits landed after it (f5b8e2f..2aad4dd), including substantial undocumented feature work: device-line v1.2 fragmentation (9799b1e), restart-free declarative rebind (b32ba10), the AIP receive decision table wired into desktop/iOS (e2179d5, d941a9e, 050bac7, 1c8c2fa), unresolved-stop surfacing (4329c1e, bc6d834, d7199a8), MAINTAINERS-MAP (2b5c640), deprecation-ledger (ea2aef9), the architecture-checks single entrypoint (3c0fda3), the AGENTS.md rewrite itself (160d880, 248e120), and all five drills plus their fix-up commit (d391f38, 3b0af66, 75a6f27, 713f8fe, 2aad4dd). The progress file's own §3 still reads "本輪已收尾" (this round is wrapped up) with a completed-items list that predates all of this. AGENTS.md was itself introduced this branch as a standalone file replacing a CLAUDE.md symlink (commits 160d880/248e120), so this stale cross-reference is a defect of this branch's own diff, not pre-existing.

One nuance that doesn't rescue the finding but is worth recording: `docs/releases/v0.7.0-progress.md` does exist on a sibling worktree/branch `wt/docs-final` (commit 07d3d01, not an ancestor of this branch's HEAD) — so the fallback clause "若檔案還不在，以上一份為準" is a real, in-progress transitional state, not pure fiction. But that file's own section numbering is §0/§1/§2/§3/§4(已完成步驟)/§5(下一動作)/§6(Blockers) — Blockers is §6 there, not §4. So AGENTS.md's "§4（Blockers）與 §5" instruction is correct only for file (a) today, and will point at the wrong sections once file (b) is merged in as-is. This reinforces rather than refutes the finding: the §7 pointer is fragile/already wrong in one dimension (missing §5 in file (a)) and set up to be wrong in a different way once (b) lands, and neither current-branch state has a coherent §4+§5 pair.

Net: the finding's central claim — a new session following AGENTS.md §7 today lands on a stale, section-mismatched fallback document that undercounts real progress by ~29 commits' worth of shipped work — is verified true against the current tree.

confirmed.fix: 把 §7 改成「先讀 §4（Blockers）」（拿掉 §5），或在 progress 文件補一個 §5；並把本輪的完成項與新的 blockers 回填進 v0.6.x-maintainability-progress.md（或依 AGENTS.md 的承諾建立 v0.7.0-progress.md）。
confirmed.regressionTest: A docs-claims style lint (scripts/tests/docs-claims.sh) check: for each `progress.md` file named in AGENTS.md §7, (1) assert the file exists or the AGENTS.md line explicitly says so, and (2) if it exists, assert it contains a `## 4.` section whose heading matches the parenthetical label AGENTS.md cites (here "Blockers") and a `## 5.` section — failing loudly (not silently) whenever the referenced section is absent or renumbered, so the fallback file and the pointer can't drift independently. Separately, add a staleness guard comparing the progress file's last-recorded commit SHA (from its §2/§4 "已完成步驟" entries) against `git rev-list --count <that-sha>..HEAD`, failing/warning above a threshold to force a progress-file refresh before it's trusted as the resume point.

confirmed.title: docs-claims.sh 對 CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 的 Known limitations 零覆蓋，過期宣稱檢查也只在「同一行且帶 v 前綴」時才生效
confirmed.file: scripts/tests/docs-claims.sh:171 (stale_docs list excludes CHANGELOG.md/docs/releases/*), :189 (stale_words missing "準備中"), :192-193 (same-line "v"+ver requirement) — the cited :163 is the start of the same code block (evidence-index check) so is in the right place, just not the tightest anchor
confirmed.claim: 這支 lint 是本分支宣稱用來擋過期文件宣稱的關卡（release-verify.sh:100 直接跑它，architecture-checks.sh 的 docs 組也跑它），但它的 CHANGELOG 檢查只有兩件事：最上層段不得含固定字串「在落地前不會出現在這裡」，以及三個硬編碼功能名要出現在 `## [0.6.0]` 段。Known limitations 一個字都不看——所以上面第 1 條那兩條已經是假的已知限制存在時，這支 lint 仍然 107 passed / 0 failed。另一半（已發布版本的過期措辭）也比它自己的註解宣稱的弱：`if ("v" + ver) in line` 要求版本字串**帶 v 前綴且與過期詞同一行**，因此「0.6.0 目前仍在候選階段」（無 v）、或版本與過期詞被斷成兩行，都不會被抓；`stale_words` 八個詞也遺漏了這個 repo 自己在用的「準備中」——`apps/interaction-desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:4117` 的 fixture 就是 `## [0.5.0] — 2026-09-03（準備中）`，正是 release prep 會留下的形狀。
confirmed.evidence: 實跑 `bash scripts/tests/docs-claims.sh` → 「docs-claims: 107 passed / 0 failed」，同時 CHANGELOG.md:212／:223 的兩條已知限制在 HEAD 上為假（見第 1 條的反證）。lint 邏輯：:163 `stale_words = ("尚未 tag", "尚未發布", "尚未落地", "候選版本", "候選", "進行中", "開發中", "未發布")`；:165-167 `for line in text.splitlines(): if ("v" + ver) in line: hit = [w for w in stale_words if w in line]`。檢查範圍只有 `stale_docs = [README.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/FEATURES.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md]`（:163 上一行），不含 CHANGELOG.md、docs/acceptance-evidence.md、docs/releases/*。

verdicts.reasoning:
Read scripts/tests/docs-claims.sh in full and independently verified every mechanical claim:

1. Zero coverage of "Known limitations" content: grepped the script for 已知限制/Known limitations/known-limitations — zero hits. The only check touching the CHANGELOG's topmost section (lines 34-71, `unreleased = topmost_section(ch)`) only asserts the boilerplate string "在落地前不會出現在這裡" is absent and that three specific landed features have entries in `## [0.6.0]`; it never reads or validates the "### Known limitations" bullets against actual repo state. So if any Known-limitations bullet is stale, this lint cannot catch it — confirmed as literally zero coverage.

2. Weak stale-claim check for released versions (lines 161-195): `stale_docs` (line 171) is exactly `["README.md","docs/ARCHITECTURE.md","docs/FEATURES.md","CLAUDE.md","AGENTS.md"]` — CHANGELOG.md, docs/releases/*, and docs/acceptance-evidence.md are excluded from this check entirely. And the per-line matching (`if ("v"+ver) in line`) really does require the literal "v"+version substring and a stale word on the *same* line of text. I ran a standalone Python simulation reproducing the exact logic:
   - "0.6.0 目前仍在候選階段" (no `v` prefix) → not checked at all.
   - Version and stale word on separate lines → not checked.
   - "v0.6.0 目前仍在候選階段" (same line, v-prefixed) → correctly caught.
   This confirms the same-line + v-prefix requirement exactly as claimed.

3. `stale_words` (line 189) tuple is `("尚未 tag","尚未發布","尚未落地","候選版本","候選","進行中","開發中","未發布")` — "準備中" is absent. Simulated a line "## [v0.5.0] — 2026-09-03（準備中）" (v-prefixed, same line) through the exact check logic: it is inspected (passes the "v"+ver gate) but produces `hit=[]` because "準備中" isn't in the word list — so it would silently pass even in the one code path designed to catch this class of staleness.

4. Verified apps/interaction-desktop/src-tauri/lib.rs:4117 area does contain the literal fixture string `"## [0.5.0] — 2026-09-03（準備中）"` in `changelog_topmost_section_follows_a_renamed_heading`, matching the finding's cited evidence that "準備中" is a real, in-repo vocabulary word for exactly this release-prep shape — making the gap concrete rather than hypothetical.

5. Confirmed release-verify.sh:100-101 runs docs-claims.sh as a hard `gate` (not skip/warn), and architecture-checks.sh:66/103 also wires it in — matching the finding's framing that this is a release-blocking lint.

6. Ran `bash scripts/tests/docs-claims.sh` — it exits 0 with "111 passed / 0 failed" (finding said 107; the small count difference is immaterial and likely reflects additional evidence-index entries added since the finding was drafted — it doesn't change the substance: the script still passes cleanly with these gaps present).

All load-bearing technical claims (zero Known-limitations coverage, same-line+v-prefix requirement narrowing the stale-word check, missing "準備中" in the word list, exclusion of CHANGELOG.md/docs/releases from stale_docs, and the gate wiring) check out against the actual file content. I did not independently re-verify whether the two cited Known-limitations bullets (CHANGELOG.md:212, :223) are themselves already false — that is a different finding's claim — but the core assertion here (the lint mechanically cannot detect such staleness even if it exists) stands on its own regardless of that other finding's outcome.

confirmed.fix: (a) 新增一段「已知限制對帳」：把 CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` §Known limitations 的每一條綁一個可執行斷言（例如「宣稱 needs-restart-to-rebind 存在」時要求 `rg needs-restart-to-rebind crates/` 有命中，反之則紅）；(b) 過期詞比對改成同時接受帶／不帶 `v` 前綴、比對範圍放大到段落而非單行，並把「準備中」「未 tag」「pre-release」「RC」加進 stale_words。

verdicts.reasoning:
Tried hard to refute and could not. Verified every empirical claim independently:

1. Repro command: `rg -n 'syncProfile|characterSessionSync' apps/interaction-desktop/src apps/interaction-ios` on the reviewed HEAD returns 45 hits across 9 files, not 0 — and the per-file breakdown matches the finding exactly (api.ts:4, CharacterSyncCard.tsx:3, ConnectPage.tsx:3, characterSync.ts:12, character-sync-card.test.tsx:2, connectPage.test.tsx:4, regressions-v06-general-mode.test.tsx:1, regressions-v06-round2-general-mode.test.tsx:1, statusProjection-session.test.ts:15).

2. Code check: `apps/interaction-desktop/src/statusProjection/characterSync.ts:634-637` explicitly checks `characterSyncProfileLabel(m.syncProfile) !== null` (true for `intent-only`/`event-source`) and returns `"partial-sync"` *before* the `canPresent`/role-based `partial-capability` branch — directly contradicting the drill doc's claim that only `role` and negotiated intents decide "已同步" and that `intent-only` renders as synced.

3. Test check: `apps/interaction-desktop/src/test/statusProjection-session.test.ts:703-710` (`it("online 但只接收指令／只回報事件：不是「已同步」，也不給綠勾"`) asserts `p.state === "partial-sync"` for exactly this scenario. Ran it directly: `npx vitest run src/test/statusProjection-session.test.ts -t "online 但只接收指令"` → 1 passed.

4. History check: this wiring (`syncProfile` read from `/v1/status` and `/v1/character-session/diagnostics`, threaded into `characterSync.ts`, `api.ts`, `ConnectPage.tsx`, `CharacterSyncCard.tsx`) was added in commit `bc6d834` ("feat(desktop): say what each device member actually gets, and let a stopped device be re-enabled"), which sits 8 commits *before* `713f8fe` (the drill doc's own commit) in `git log --reverse f5b8e2f..2aad4dd`. So the doc's "0 命中" claim was already false at the moment it was written, not just stale by the time of review.

5. Confirmed the false text is still present verbatim at the cited location: `docs/releases/v0.7.0-drills.md:408-409` still reads the `rg` command followed by "（0 命中）", and a later commit on this same branch (`2aad4dd`, "fix(maintainability): 把演練找到的七個缺口變成可執行的把關") touched `device-profile.md`, the regression test's `PENDING_GUIDE_ROWS`, and `docs-claims.sh`, but did **not** touch `v0.7.0-drills.md` — so the false repro/conclusion in F3 was never corrected even though the surrounding gap-closing commit landed on top of it.

Everything in the finding's evidence block is independently reproducible and accurate: the mechanism (`syncProfile` gating `partial-sync`) is real, tested, predates the drill commit, and the doc's own "not speculation" reproduction is objectively wrong on both the hit-count and the UI-outcome claims.

confirmed.fix: F3 改寫成它真正還成立的那一半（＝上一條 finding：diagnostics 讀不到時仍會綠勾），刪掉「0 命中」與 intent-only→已同步 的表格，或在每一列標明「觀察於 <commit>，之後已由 <commit> 改變」。文件開頭已經承諾「一律用檔案路徑引用」，那就必須用 HEAD 的檔案內容重跑一次再落筆。
confirmed.regressionTest: Not applicable to app code (the bug is in a documentation file, not runtime behavior — the runtime behavior it mis-describes is already correctly covered by the existing `statusProjection-session.test.ts:703-710` test). The fix is a doc edit: replace the F3 section in docs/releases/v0.7.0-drills.md with either (a) an acknowledgment that `syncProfile` already gates `partial-sync` in `characterSync.ts` (citing the real line numbers and the existing regression test), or (b) drop F3 entirely if it no longer represents a real gap. If maintainers want a guard against this class of doc rot, `scripts/tests/docs-claims.sh` could optionally assert that any `rg` hit-count literally quoted in a shipped doc still matches (à la the ledger self-count check already added in 2aad4dd), but that is a process improvement, not a required regression test.

verdicts.reasoning:
Verified every load-bearing claim independently and could not refute any of them; the finding is confirmed, and the live file state makes it worse than originally described (an internal self-contradiction, not just staleness).

1. CLAUDE.md really does say "已知限制記錄在 CHANGELOG.md 與 docs/acceptance-evidence.md，修掉時同步更新" (confirmed in the system-prompt copy of CLAUDE.md).

2. The [Unreleased] section's self-description ("本段只記本分支（feature/v0.6.x-maintainability）已提交的變更，每條附 commit") is present at CHANGELOG.md:12-13, unchanged since the base commit.

3. Diffed the exact "### Known limitations（本分支新增；修掉時同步刪除）" block (base commit f5b8e2f lines 210-224) against the current HEAD block (now at lines 392-407, after ~180 new lines were prepended above it): byte-for-byte identical (`diff` exit 0). So "一字未改" is literally true for this block, even though the file has grown by ~200 lines since.

4. Checked each cited fix is real and lands in commits inside f5b8e2f..HEAD (all present in `git log --oneline f5b8e2f..HEAD`):
   - (a) epoch-realign unification: `crates/interaction-aip/tests/fixtures/manifest.json` fixtures `different-epoch-without-a-reset-declaration` / `smaller-epoch-without-a-reset-declaration` both now expect `decision: realign, reason: epoch-changed` (this whole fixture block is a pure `+` addition in the f5b8e2f..HEAD diff), consumed by `crates/interaction-session/tests/receive_decisions_from_json.rs`, `apps/interaction-desktop/src/test/receive-decision-fixtures.test.ts`, and `apps/interaction-ios/InteractionCompanionTests/ReceiveDecisionConformanceTests.swift` — all three files exist. Landed in commit `d941a9e` (in-branch).
   - (b) MAX_RESUME_PATCHES: `apps/interaction-desktop/src/aip/sessionClient.ts:78` is now `export const MAX_RESUME_PATCHES = AIP_LIMITS.maxResumePatches;` (no more hardcoded 1024); `crates/interaction-aip/src/limits.rs:18,42` defines `EVENT_LOG_RING = 512` and `MAX_RESUME_PATCHES = EVENT_LOG_RING` with a compile-time `const _: () = assert!(MAX_RESUME_PATCHES == EVENT_LOG_RING)`; `schemas/aip-1.0.schema.json:475` publishes `"maxResumePatches": 512`. The claimed "1024" constant does not exist anywhere in current source (only in changelog prose describing history). Landed in commit `d941a9e` (in-branch).
   - (c) iOS background-gate automated test: `apps/interaction-ios/InteractionCompanionTests/ConnectionManagerGateTests.swift` has 7 `func test` cases, added by commit `a0d3309` ("make the connection manager's socket and scheduler injectable, and test the five background gates"), with `Services/SocketTransport.swift` as the injectable seam — commit is in-branch.
   - (d) Disabled→Available rebind without restart: `crates/interaction-runtime/src/declarative_lifecycle.rs` added by commit `b32ba10`; regression tests `reenable_rebinds_without_restart` (declarative_session_loop.rs:1401) and `mqtt_reenable_rebinds_without_restart` (mqtt_rebind_loop.rs:175) both exist — commit in-branch.
   - Serial snapshot/members gap: `crates/interaction-adapter-declarative/src/fragment.rs` (443 lines, device-wire v1.2) added by commit `9799b1e`; the cited test `a_fragmenting_device_receives_the_snapshot_and_is_a_full_state_member` does exist (in `crates/interaction-runtime/tests/declarative_session_loop.rs:1720`, not in fragment.rs itself as the finding's evidence slightly mis-locates it, but the test is real and was added by the same in-branch commit `9799b1e`) — a minor citation imprecision, not a defect in the underlying claim.

5. Went further than the finding: the *current* HEAD (which has advanced past the finding's 28-commit snapshot to 40 commits) has since prepended a new "本輪（v0.7.0 候選）" subsection to the very same still-open [Unreleased] block. That new subsection explicitly says "已修掉、從清單移除的三條…" and strikes through (a), (d), and the Serial-snapshot limitation with commit citations, and separately documents the (b) MAX_RESUME_PATCHES fix (line 34-35, 95) and the (c) ConnectionManager test fix (line 77) in its own Added/Changed sections. Yet the OLD paragraph at line 392-407 was never deleted or annotated as superseded — so the same document now asserts, in two places, both "these are known limitations, unfixed" and "these were fixed here". This is a stronger, more concrete instance of the defect than the original finding could even see (it only had the 28-commit snapshot), and it directly falsifies the file's own "誠實階梯" spirit: a reader reconciling CHANGELOG against reality gets an active contradiction, not just a stale claim.

I found no disclaimer marking the old block as historical/superseded, no re-dating separating the two subsections' scope, and no test or lint (docs-claims.sh) that would have caught this internal inconsistency — `docs-claims.sh`'s known check (per CHANGELOG:97-98) is scoped to blocking stale "not yet tagged" phrasing on published-version strings, not to reconciling known-limitations checkboxes against fix commits.

Severity: keeping "medium" — this is a documentation-accuracy / process-discipline defect (violates the CLAUDE.md rule to update known limitations when fixed, and undermines the "誠實階梯"/evidence-reconciliation purpose of the CHANGELOG), not a runtime correctness or safety-invariant violation, so it doesn't rise to high/blocker under this repo's severity conventions.

The right regression guard is a docs-lint addition to `scripts/tests/docs-claims.sh` (or a new check) that: for every commit SHA cited in an "Added/Fixed/Changed" bullet under the same still-open `## [Unreleased]` section, greps the rest of that same section's "Known limitations" bullets for language that a maintainer tags as closed-by that SHA (e.g. requiring a `~~struck-through~~` + commit reference, as the newer "已修掉、從清單移除" convention already does), and fails if a Known-limitations bullet's referenced commit-window overlaps a Fixed-bullet's cited SHA without a matching strikethrough/removal — i.e., mechanically catch "the same file says both fixed and not-fixed for the same commit."

verdicts.reasoning:
Independently reproduced the core claim. `grep -cE 'tokio::test|#\[test\]' crates/interaction-runtime/tests/declarative_session_loop.rs` = 26 at HEAD (26 `#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]` attributes, listed lines match exactly what the finding cites). Cross-checked all four documents:
- docs/aip/device-profile.md:133 — still says "13 測" (verbatim: `declarative_session_loop.rs`（13 測；D1 的 7 支加上 D2 的…). Confirmed via `git diff f5b8e2f..HEAD -- docs/aip/device-profile.md`: this exact line carries neither `-` nor `+` in the diff even though the file gained +177 lines in this range (a large new §6.1 rebind section was inserted nearby) — so the branch edited this file but left the stale count untouched.
- docs/aip/transport-bindings.md:310 — says "25 測". The diff shows this line WAS edited within this branch's range (from "13 測" to "25 測"), so it was updated once but not kept in sync after later commits pushed the real count to 26 — an off-by-one drift introduced by the branch's own later commits.
- docs/acceptance-evidence.md:944 — says "13 測". This file is untouched in the f5b8e2f..HEAD diff, but the number it references became more wrong because of this branch's own commits to the test file (it was already 15 at scope-start, now 26).
- docs/releases/v0.7.0-drills.md:148 — correctly says "26 passed / 0 failed…新增前是 25 支", i.e. this is the only document in sync with the real file.
CHANGELOG.md lines 44/58 independently corroborate that a prior adversarial-review round (`427c806`) had already caught and fixed this exact class of drift for device-profile.md, moving the stated count from 7→13 — so the same drift pattern reappearing in the same branch is a real, verifiable recurrence, not speculation.

One part of the finding is an overreach and I could not confirm it: the claim that `mqtt_rebind_loop.rs` contradicts "MQTT／BLE 沒有 AIP session 測試" doesn't hold up under inspection. I read the full test (`mqtt_reenable_rebinds_without_restart`) and its fake-device handler: the simulated device only answers `who`/`read`/`stop-all` message types, and `grep -rn '"aip"'` across `mqtt_rebind_loop.rs` and `interaction-adapter-declarative/tests/mqtt_loop.rs` returns nothing — neither file ever sends or receives a `{"type":"aip",...}` envelope. The new test exercises the transport-agnostic pairing/rebind lifecycle (`DeclarativeLifecycle`, `provider.rebound` audit) over MQTT, not the AIP session envelope protocol itself (touch/broadcast/outbound-registry, which is what `declarative_session_loop.rs`'s "AIP session tests" actually cover for serial, and what `aip_link.rs`'s `MockRawLink` covers generically). So the transport-bindings.md/device-profile.md statement that MQTT/BLE share `AipChannel<L>` but have no AIP session test remains literally accurate even after this addition — this sub-claim in the finding should be treated as not established, though it doesn't undermine the (separately well-evidenced) numeric-drift claim, which is the finding's actual title and main content.

Reproduced the exact schemars 1.x output for the two shapes the claim says are missed. Built a scratch crate pinned to the same `schemars = "1"` requirement as the workspace (resolved to 1.2.2, the same major used by interaction-session); `schema_for!` on a struct with a `BTreeMap<String, f64>` field produces `{"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"number",...}}`, and on a `(f64, f64)` tuple field produces `{"type":"array","prefixItems":[{"type":"number",...},...]}` — i.e. schemars 1.x really does use `additionalProperties` for maps and `prefixItems` (not `items`) for fixed tuples.

There is no branch for `additionalProperties` or `prefixItems`, so for the two probed shapes the `"type":"number"` check at lines 354-361 is on a subtree the function never visits — the number-typed leaf is provably unreachable, not just unlikely to be reached. `rg additionalProperties|prefixItems` in the file (and `git show HEAD:...` for it) confirms zero hits, matching the finding's own check.

Confirmed the file is otherwise pre-existing: `git diff f5b8e2f..HEAD` shows only a pure-append hunk (+251 lines) starting after the original line 546; `collect_double_paths` (line 332, well before 546) is byte-identical to the base version — so this is not a regression this branch introduced, exactly as the finding itself states. I did find one small inaccuracy in the finding's framing: it calls the new `collect_field_paths()` gate '工作區中未提交的' (uncommitted in the working tree), but `git log --follow` shows it already landed in commit 2aad4dd, which is inside this branch's base..HEAD diff range (HEAD moved 29 commits past the stated base while this review ran). That doesn't touch the core claim — I independently verified `collect_field_paths` (the new gate added in this branch) has the identical missing-branches shape, so the branch did in fact freshly copy the same blind-spot pattern into new code, which if anything makes the observation more in-scope, not less.

Verified the downstream chain precisely: generated.ts:333-336 and docs/aip/README.md:340 and docs/aip/conformance.md:67 all state, in the cited wording, that a new f64 field not covered by codegen "會被 pnpm aip:check 擋下" — an overclaim for map/tuple-shaped fields per the above. Confirmed apps/interaction-desktop/src/aip/sessionClient.ts:70/568 that `REALIGN_STREAK_LIMIT = AIP_LIMITS.maxRealignAttempts`, and generated.ts:354 sets `maxRealignAttempts: 3`, so "connected three times to unrecoverable" is accurate. Ran `cargo test -p interaction-session --test state_hash_fixtures state_hash_fixtures_are_what_the_host_writes` — passes today (SemanticState has no map/tuple f64 field yet, so the gate is not currently broken; the defect is latent, triggered only by a future field addition), consistent with the finding's own framing as a dormant gap rather than an active failure. All cited line numbers (332 for the function; 333-336, README:340, conformance.md:67) matched exactly on inspection; the two assertion-block line numbers were off by one (478→479) but point to the same two `assert_eq!` calls, an immaterial drift.

confirmed.fix: 在 `collect_double_paths`（與工作區新加的 `collect_field_paths`）補上 `additionalProperties` → `{pointer}/*` 與 `prefixItems` → `{pointer}/{i}` 兩條遞迴；TS 端的 `buildPathTrie` 已經支援 `*` 萬用段，不必改。另外把「深度超過 16 就 `return`」從靜默跳過改成 panic，否則深巢狀同樣會靜默漏掉。

confirmed.title: accept_fragment 只擋「明確宣告了 caps 卻沒有 aip.frag/1」的裝置，沒有 caps 的舊韌體送分片一樣收——與自身註解與 device-profile §6.3 的說法不符
confirmed.file: crates/interaction-adapter-declarative/src/protocol.rs:636 (guard in accept_fragment); root cause is advertises() at :824 returning None for a handshaken-but-empty-caps device, fed by store_caps() being called unconditionally (including with an empty vec) around :989-999; contrast outbound gate at :720 which uses == Some(true) and so is NOT permissive for the same no-caps case. Doc mismatch: docs/aip/device-profile.md §6.3 (~line 261-262).
confirmed.claim: `accept_fragment` 的守門是 `if self.advertises(FRAG_CAP) == Some(false)`。`advertises()` 在「裝置 hello 完全沒有宣告 caps」時回 `None`（舊韌體相容），於是這種裝置送進來的 `aip-frag` 會被照單全收並開始重組。這與同一函式上方的註解「分片來自**沒有宣告** FRAG_CAP 的裝置時一律拒絕：它沒說自己會分片，我們就不替它猜（能力宣告是這條線唯一的能力事實）」以及 docs/aip/device-profile.md §6.3「沒宣告卻送分片進來的裝置在 `accept_fragment` 就被拒絕」都不一致；也與**出站**方向不對稱——`supports_fragmentation()` 用的是 `== Some(true)`，`None` 一律當成「做不到」。
confirmed.evidence: protocol.rs:636 `if self.advertises(FRAG_CAP) == Some(false) {`（入站）對比 protocol.rs:720 `self.advertises(FRAG_CAP) == Some(true)`（出站）；protocol.rs:820-830 `advertises()`：`let caps = self.caps_snapshot()?;`（沒握手／沒 caps → None）`if caps.is_empty() { return None; }`。註解在 protocol.rs:630-634。docs/aip/device-profile.md §6.3：「沒宣告卻送分片進來的裝置在 `protocol.rs:635`＝`accept_fragment` 就被拒絕」。實際影響有界（重組緩衝仍受 8 KiB／64 片／2 秒逾時保護），但它是一條與宣稱不符的放行路徑。

verdicts.reasoning:
Traced the full call chain by hand (no reliance on the finding's own narrative):

1. `DeviceLink::admit_aip` (protocol.rs:589) only reaches `accept_fragment` after `handshake_ready()` is true, i.e. after `ensure_ready_generation`'s hello/pair sequence has completed.
2. That handshake path (around protocol.rs:988-999) calls `self.store_caps(caps)` **unconditionally** — even when `caps.is_empty()` it only logs a debug line ("capability gating disabled for it") and still stores the (empty) vec. So by the time any `aip`/`aip-frag` message can be admitted, `advertised_caps` is always `Some(_)`, never the pre-handshake `None`.
3. `advertises()` (protocol.rs:824): `let caps = self.caps_snapshot()?;` then `if caps.is_empty() { return None; }`. So a device that completed handshake but declared no caps (or an empty caps list — the "old firmware" case the code comments explicitly call out) yields `advertises(FRAG_CAP) == None`, exactly like a device that never handshook at all.
4. `accept_fragment` (protocol.rs:635-636) only rejects when `self.advertises(FRAG_CAP) == Some(false)` — i.e. only devices that declared a *non-empty* caps list lacking `aip.frag/1`. A device with no/empty caps gets `None`, the `if` is false, and execution falls through into the reassembler (`self.reassembly_guard().accept(...)`), i.e. the fragment is buffered/processed exactly as if fragmentation had been declared.

This directly contradicts the doc-comment immediately above the function ("分片來自**沒有宣告** FRAG_CAP 的裝置時一律拒絕") and docs/aip/device-profile.md §6.3's blanket claim ("沒宣告卻送分片進來的裝置在 accept_fragment 就被拒絕") — both state an unconditional rejection that the code does not implement for the no-caps-declared case.

Cross-checked the asymmetry claim too: `supports_fragmentation()` (protocol.rs:720) uses `== Some(true)`, so for the same no-caps device it correctly returns `false` (outbound fragmentation withheld) — confirming the outbound and inbound paths use inconsistent None-handling for the same capability.

Confirmed this is genuinely untested: grepped `crates/interaction-adapter-declarative/tests/` for `not-advertised` and for any `AipFrag`-related test that constructs a device with empty/no caps — every existing fragmentation test (`aip_link.rs`, `aip_fragment.rs`) declares caps as `vec!["led.set".into(), FRAG_CAP.into()]`; none exercises a device with `caps: vec![]` sending an `AipFrag`. So the gap is real, reachable by construction, and has zero test coverage.

Confirmed this is in-scope for this branch: `git log` shows `accept_fragment`/`AipFrag`/`FragmentDropped` were introduced by commit 9799b1e ("feat(device-line): fragment AIP envelopes over the wire (v1.2)") within this branch's range (f5b8e2f..HEAD); `advertises()`/`caps_snapshot()` themselves are pre-existing and unchanged (confirmed via `git show f5b8e2f:...` — identical body), reused from the established outbound-gating convention (`link_caps.rs:407`, `protocol.rs:1120` also use `== Some(false)` for the same "old firmware = permissive" outbound reasoning). The bug is that this outbound convention was copy-pasted onto an inbound trust decision where the stated intent (and the doc) is the opposite: unconditional rejection for undeclared capability.

Impact is genuinely bounded as the finding says: even if admitted, reassembly is still capped by the pre-existing 8 KiB / 64-fragment / 2-second-timeout protections (fragment.rs), and completing reassembly only ever yields the same `AipAdmission::Admitted(envelope)` a plain unfragmented `Aip` message would produce — no privilege beyond what any handshaken device can already send in one line. So this is a doc/comment-vs-code inconsistency with low practical severity, not an amplification of trust, matching the reported "low" severity.

confirmed.fix: 把入站守門改成 `if self.advertises(FRAG_CAP) != Some(true)`（與出站對稱），並在 drop reason 上保留 `not-advertised`；或把註解與 §6.3 改成誠實描述「沒有宣告 caps 的舊韌體不受此閘門保護」。
confirmed.regressionTest: In crates/interaction-adapter-declarative/tests/aip_link.rs, add a test using `MockRawLink::with_caps("esp32-01", None, vec![], Some(639))` (empty caps = old-firmware/no-declaration), call `link.ensure_ready().await`, then build a 2-fragment `DeviceMsg::AipFrag` via `fragment_envelope_line` and feed the first fragment to `link.admit_aip(&frame)`. Assert the result is `Some(AipAdmission::FragmentDropped(drop))` with `drop.reason == "not-advertised"` (per the accept_fragment/doc intent) — today's code instead returns `Some(AipAdmission::FragmentBuffered)`, which would fail such an assertion and pins the gap.

confirmed.title: pending_fragment_drop 是單一槽：第二次取消會覆蓋掉還沒被取走的第一筆稽核
confirmed.file: crates/interaction-adapter-declarative/src/protocol.rs:668,692,701-703 (write/drain sites); crates/interaction-runtime/src/declarative_session.rs:425 (sole drain call site), :656/:583 (concurrent stop_all entry point via SensorSource::request_stop)
confirmed.claim: `cancel_reassembly()` 與 `accept_fragment()` 的 superseded 路徑都直接 `*lock_ignoring_poison(&self.pending_fragment_drop) = Some(drop)`，不檢查槽裡有沒有還沒被 `expire_fragments()` 取走的舊值。收訊迴圈每輪最多取走一筆（`expire_fragments` 取到 pending 就 early return），所以在同一個 RX_POLL 窗（400 ms）內發生兩次丟棄時，先發生的那一筆稽核會被靜默覆蓋——違反 fragment.rs 模組文件「不靜默：每一次丟棄都回傳一個 FragmentDrop，呼叫端負責留稽核」。
confirmed.evidence: protocol.rs:668（superseded 路徑）與 protocol.rs:692（cancel 路徑）都是無條件覆寫；protocol.rs:701-703 `if let Some(pending) = lock_ignoring_poison(&self.pending_fragment_drop).take() { return Some(pending); }`——一輪只吐一筆。呼叫點 declarative_session.rs:424 每輪只呼叫一次 `expire_fragments()`，而該迴圈的節奏是 `RX_POLL = 400ms`（declarative_session.rs:55）或收到訊息時。fragment.rs:21 的承諾：「**不靜默**：每一次丟棄都回傳一個 FragmentDrop，呼叫端負責留稽核」。

verdicts.reasoning:
Verified end-to-end against the current file contents (no line drift of substance).

Mechanism (protocol.rs): `pending_fragment_drop: std::sync::Mutex<Option<FragmentDrop>>` (line 480) is written unconditionally with no check for an existing unclaimed value at two sites — the superseded path inside `accept_fragment` (line 668, `*lock_ignoring_poison(&self.pending_fragment_drop) = Some(dropped);`) and `cancel_reassembly` (line 692, same pattern). `expire_fragments` drains it with a single `.take()` (lines 701-703) and returns at most one `FragmentDrop` per call — confirmed by its own early-return shape. `cancel_reassembly` itself is invoked from five distinct call sites whose own return value is always discarded (`admit_aip`'s not-paired branch at 597, `ensure_ready_generation`'s hello reset at 881, `invalidate_handshake` at 1017, `stop_all` at 1388, `LinkShutdown::shutdown` at 1590) — every one of them relies solely on a *later, separate* `expire_fragments()` call to ever surface the drop; none self-drains.

Sole drain point: `declarative_session.rs:425` calls `expire_fragments()` exactly once per iteration of the per-device `run()` background loop (spawned once via `tokio::spawn(binding.run())` at line 816), after processing at most one inbound message per iteration. RX_POLL=400ms (line 53) only bounds the idle case; when a message arrives, drain follows almost immediately after `on_aip(...).await` returns.

Cross-task writers are real, not hypothetical: `stop_all()` is reached via `SensorSource::request_stop` (declarative_session.rs:656, trait impl at line 583), which is dispatched by the runtime's sensor-stop/emergency-stop machinery — a call path entirely independent of, and running concurrently with, the device's own `run()` task. `LinkShutdown::shutdown()` (protocol.rs:1584-1590) is reachable from provider disable/revoke/rebind flows, likewise a different task. Both write into the same slot the `run()` loop also writes into, with no coordination beyond the raw mutex's per-assignment critical section.

Concrete loss scenario: `run()`'s task writes a supersede drop into the slot (inside the synchronous `admit_aip` call), then awaits inside `on_aip(...)` (e.g. `character_session_device_frame(...).await`, `send_aip(...).await` for a completed/admitted envelope) before reaching the line-425 drain. If, during that await window (or, under a real multi-threaded tokio runtime, at any overlapping wall-clock instant), a concurrently-running `stop_all()`/`shutdown()`/`invalidate_handshake()` call on another task also writes to the slot, the run() loop's own `expire_fragments()` call afterward returns only the second writer's drop; the first is gone with no way to retrieve it (the reassembly buffer for that xfer was already cleared at cancellation time, so nothing else remembers it).

No existing test covers this: `aip_link.rs`'s `a_reconnect_cancels_an_in_flight_inbound_transfer` only asserts a single drop isn't double-reported (`expire_fragments()` called twice returns Some-then-None) — it never exercises two distinct drop-producing events landing before a single drain. I confirmed this is also a deterministic, purely single-threaded reproduction path (not just a timing-dependent race): three overlapping fragmented transfers (xfer1 buffered, xfer2 supersedes xfer1 without an intervening `expire_fragments()`, xfer3 supersedes xfer2 without an intervening `expire_fragments()`) lose xfer1's drop unconditionally, regardless of scheduling — `accept()` in fragment.rs (lines 299-315) confirms each supersede independently calls `self.cancel("superseded")` and unconditionally overwrites, with no queueing.

This is new code entirely introduced in this branch (commit 9799b1e, the v1.2 fragmentation feature) — not pre-existing code the branch merely touched — so it is squarely in scope.

Severity: I agree with "low" as claimed. The loss is confined to one `aip.fragment-dropped` audit-log entry; it does not affect the actual device/session behavior, does not leak the in-memory reassembly buffer (already cleared at cancellation regardless of whether the audit trail records it), and does not touch any safety-critical path (Policy Governor ceilings, estop irreversibility, consent). It is a genuine violation of fragment.rs's documented "不靜默" invariant, but a narrow one requiring two independent drop-causing events to coincide within a small, undrained window.

confirmed.fix: 改成有界的小佇列（例如 `VecDeque` 上限 4~8），滿了就記一筆「還有 N 筆未回報」的彙總；或讓 `expire_fragments()` 一次回傳 `Vec<FragmentDrop>`，呼叫端逐筆稽核。

confirmed.title: e2e 任務 11 的 else 分支沒有取消任何東西，卻仍被記成「取消進行中的工作 completed」
confirmed.file: apps/interaction-desktop/e2e/general-mode-tasks.spec.ts:1123-1137 (else branch at 1131-1136; record() call at 1137)
confirmed.claim: 任務 11 在找不到「暫停／中斷目前工作」按鈕時走 else：只按「關閉」把工作階段關掉，接著仍以 `record(m, { actual: "completed" })` 記成完成。此時後端不會出現 `cancelled`，而 docs/releases/v0.6.x-general-mode-tasks.md §1 第 12 列明確宣稱「按『暫停／中斷目前工作』→ 後端 `cancelled`」。兩條路徑的決策數都是 5，§2.1 的量測表也分辨不出來，TASK_MANIFEST 的漂移防線同樣抓不到——一個沒做到的任務可以合法地拿到 completed。
confirmed.evidence: apps/interaction-desktop/e2e/general-mode-tasks.spec.ts:1123-1136：if 分支才 `waitSessionState(..., ["cancelled"], ...)`；else 分支只 `m.decide("關閉這個工作階段")` ＋ 斷言「工作階段已關閉」，1137 行仍 `await record(m, { actual: "completed" })`。TASK_MANIFEST（119 行）對「取消進行中的工作」只宣告 `expected: "completed"`，record() 對 completed 不要求任何後端證據（只對 correctly-blocked 要求前後 JSON 相同）。目前 fixture 以 `turns` 模式啟動（1094 行 makeWorkdir(..., "turns")），crates/interaction-runtime/tests/fixtures/fake_codex.sh 在該模式下會停在 inProgress，所以實務上多半走 if 分支——但這條 else 一旦成立就是靜默的假 completed。

verdicts.reasoning:
Verified line-by-line against the current file. apps/interaction-desktop/e2e/general-mode-tasks.spec.ts:1123-1137 (任務 11) is exactly as claimed: the `if (await interrupt.isVisible().catch(() => false))` branch is the only one that asserts anything about the backend (waitSessionState(...,["cancelled"],...) at 1128, and the "已取消" badge at 1130); the `} else {` branch at 1131 only clicks "關閉" (calling api.agentSessionClose(id,"closed") per apps/interaction-desktop/src/pages/AiPage.tsx:670-683) and asserts the UI text "工作階段已關閉…", with no backend-state assertion at all. Both paths fall through to the identical `await record(m, { actual: "completed" })` at line 1137.

Checked record() (general-mode-tasks.spec.ts:294-333): for `actual === "completed"` it only asserts `outcome.blocked` is undefined and that decision count is within target — it requires zero backend evidence for "completed" (evidence is only demanded for `correctly-blocked`). TASK_MANIFEST (line ~127) declares 取消進行中的工作 as `expected: "completed"` with no sub-classification, so both branches satisfy the manifest identically and no drift-detection catches the difference. docs/releases/v0.6.x-general-mode-tasks.md line 48 (row 12) explicitly claims "按『暫停／中斷目前工作』→ 後端 `cancelled`" as the completed evidence, which is only true for the if-branch.

Confirmed the else branch is not merely a theoretical dead branch: `open` (interrupt visible) is computed from `isOpenWorkState(record.state)`, which is false for `record.state === "unknown"` (apps/interaction-desktop/src/statusProjection/workState.ts: "unknown" has kind "unknown", not in OPEN_WORK_KINDS), while `closable` (the "關閉" button) is true for state "unknown" (`["failed","unknown","timed-out"].includes(record.state)`). The test's own initial `waitSessionState(...,["active","claimed-completed","waiting-for-consent","unknown"],...)` at line 1112-1118 explicitly treats "unknown" as an acceptable outcome of the initial wait — i.e. the authors already anticipated the daemon can report state "unknown" this early — so the else branch is a genuinely reachable path, not dead code, even though under the current "turns" fixture mode (fake_codex.sh never self-completes and stays `inProgress` until interrupted) the if-branch is what happens in normal runs, as the finding itself concedes.

Checked provenance: git diff f5b8e2fc9e86d8fa8067f91303dbbcb8d04cf42f..HEAD shows this exact if/else block (interrupt-vs-close, same comments, same assertions) already existed byte-for-byte pre-branch at lines 805-819, only shifted down by earlier insertions in the file. What IS new in this branch is the entire TASK_MANIFEST/`record(m, {actual, ...})` honesty-classification system itself — the base version's `record()` (base line 124: `async function record(m: TaskMetrics, options?: { maxDecisions?: number })`) had no expected/actual classification or backend-evidence requirement at all. So this branch added an anti-drift/honesty-ladder verification mechanism (exactly the kind CLAUDE.md's "誠實階梯" invariant calls for) but that new mechanism has a blind spot for the "completed" classification (it demands evidence only for "correctly-blocked"), letting this pre-existing if/else's weaker branch slip through unaudited. That satisfies "本分支的變更讓它變錯" — the new verification apparatus introduced by this branch is the thing under review, and it fails to catch this case.

No other check (general-mode-metrics.test.tsx, writeOutcomeSummary) distinguishes the two branches' evidence either. Severity "low" is appropriate: this is test/acceptance-evidence honesty, not a production safety defect, and requires the backend to actually land in a "failed/unknown/timed-out" state (or genuinely self-complete) rather than the common "turns"-fixture "active" path to manifest.

confirmed.fix: else 分支改記成 `not-run`（或另一個任務名），或直接讓它失敗：這一支任務的定義就是「取消」，沒有取消到就不該掛 completed。
confirmed.regressionTest: In record(), when outcome.actual === "completed", require a lightweight "evidence" object too (e.g. a `completedVia: "cancelled"|"closed-without-cancel"` tag) and have the doc/outcomes-JSON surface it, so 任務11's else-branch produces a visibly different evidence tag than the if-branch instead of both collapsing into the same "completed" with no evidence. Alternatively, in the test itself, assert `await waitSessionState(request, sessionId, ["closed", "failed", "timed-out", "unknown"], ...)` in the else-branch (mirroring the if-branch's ["cancelled"] wait) so the else path at least proves the backend session is actually terminal, and have record() reject a "completed" claim for this task unless that terminal-state evidence is attached.

confirmed.title: 新加的 wallClockNow 注入點只接了兩個呼叫點，註解宣稱的範圍遠大於實際
confirmed.file: apps/interaction-ios/InteractionCompanion/Services/ConnectionManager.swift:339 (declaration), with downstream effect through SessionClient.swift:711 (handleFrame's now: Date = Date() default), :430-436 (shouldResendResumeOnForeground), :512-519 (shouldAnswerHeartbeat), :1152/:1176 (resumeInFlightSince writes in sendResume/sendSnapshotQuery) — line numbers current as of HEAD, no drift found.
confirmed.claim: `wallClockNow` 的註解寫「AIP 的 occurredAt／expiresAt／resume 寬限窗用的是這一個」，但全檔只有兩處使用它（回前景 resume 與 auth-ok），所有由 inbound frame 驅動的時間判斷（intent 過期、result 的 occurredAt、heartbeat 5 秒節流、frame 觸發的 sendResume/sendSnapshotQuery 寫入的 resumeInFlightSince）仍直接用 `Date()`。結果是同一個 SessionClient 內同時存在兩個時鐘：在 ConnectionManagerGateTests 裡是 1970（注入值）與 2026（真實 Date()）並存。
confirmed.evidence: grep 全檔只有三行提到 wallClockNow：:339 宣告與註解、:547 `foregroundDidResume(now: self.wallClockNow())`、:797 `connectionDidConnect(now: self.wallClockNow(), ...)`。:763 的 `$0.handleFrame(envelope, rawFrame: text, arrivedOnGeneration: generation)` 沒有傳 `now:`，因此 SessionClient.swift:706 的 `now: Date = Date()` 預設值生效，往下影響 intentOutcome 的 `isExpired(now:)`、sendResult 的 occurredAt、handleHostHeartbeat 的節流、以及 realign 時 SessionClient.swift:1155/:1174 寫入的 `resumeInFlightSince`。ConnectionManagerGateTests.swift:187-189 注入 `Date(timeIntervalSince1970: self?.now ?? 0)`（≈1970），而同一測試裡經 socket.deliver 進來的 frame 走的是真實 2026 時鐘；`testRapidForegroundCyclesSendOneResumeUntilTheGraceWindowPasses`（:95-115）之所以成立，只是因為該測試沒有任何由 frame 觸發的 resume——一旦有，`resumeInFlightSince` 會被寫成 2026，`shouldResendResumeOnForeground`（SessionClient.swift:430-436）算出負值而走「時鐘往回跳就重問」分支，10 秒寬限窗的斷言就失去意義。

verdicts.reasoning: Verified every technical claim by reading the actual diff and code paths. `wallClockNow` is new in this branch (git diff f5b8e2f..HEAD on ConnectionManager.swift shows the whole property + its comment being added). It has exactly 3 occurrences in the file: the declaration/comment at :339, and two call sites at :547 (foregroundDidResume) and :797 (connectionDidConnect). The frame-delivery call site at :763 (`$0.handleFrame(envelope, rawFrame: text, arrivedOnGeneration: generation)`) omits `now:`, so SessionClient.handleFrame's default `now: Date = Date()` (SessionClient.swift:711) governs every inbound AIP frame. I traced that default through the whole call graph the finding names: handleCommand→SessionDecisions.intentOutcome→envelope.isExpired(now:) (intent expiry, SessionDecisions ~line 477); handleCommand's sendResult(..., now:) (result occurredAt, via WireTime.nowISO8601); handleHostHeartbeat(now:)→SessionDecisions.shouldAnswerHeartbeat(now:) (the 5s throttle, SessionClient.swift:512-519); and handleResponse→consume(now:)→the .realign branch's sendSnapshotQuery(now:)/sendResume(now:), which write `resumeInFlightSince = now` (SessionClient.swift ~1155/1174, matching the finding's cited lines). All of these use the frame path's real Date(), never wallClockNow(). Also confirmed touch()/dismiss()/intentDidFinishPlaying() are called directly from CharacterView.swift with no `now:` argument, another bypass. Confirmed ConnectionManagerGateTests.swift:187-189 overrides wallClockNow to Date(timeIntervalSince1970: ~1000) (effectively 1970) while socket.deliver() frames in the same harness are processed with real 2026 Date() — two coexisting clocks, exactly as claimed. Checked shouldResendResumeOnForeground's negative-waited branch (SessionClient.swift:430-436) and confirmed the mechanism by which a frame-triggered realign writing resumeInFlightSince with real Date() would, if compared later against the 1970 test clock, force the 'clock jumped backward' resend branch and defeat the grace-window assertion — this is a correctly-hedged latent risk (I confirmed no *existing* test currently combines a frame-triggered realign with the foreground dedup check, so no test is silently wrong today, matching the finding's careful phrasing). In production both paths default to the same real Date(), so there's no live behavioral bug outside tests, which supports the finding's own 'low' severity rather than something higher. This is a genuine, verifiable defect introduced by this branch: an incomplete injection point with an overclaiming comment and a latent test-fragility risk.

confirmed.fix: 把 `handleFrame` 也改成 `handleFrame(..., now: wallClockNow())`（SessionClient 已經有 `now` 參數），或把 :339 的註解縮到實際範圍（「只有回前景 resume 與 auth-ok」）。
confirmed.regressionTest: In ConnectionManagerGateTests.Harness, after negotiateAndSnapshot(), deliver a frame via socket.deliver() that triggers consume()'s .realign branch (e.g. a state frame with a hash mismatch or with revision/epoch that SessionDecisions.apply resolves to .realign) so sendResume/sendSnapshotQuery runs on the frame path's real Date(), writing resumeInFlightSince to the real wall-clock time. Then immediately call harness.connection.lifecyclePhaseChanged(to: .background) / .active (which uses harness.now-derived wallClockNow, e.g. ~1970) and assert sentResumes count. Today this would hit the 'waited < 0' branch in shouldResendResumeOnForeground and force an extra resume regardless of the grace window, demonstrating the two-clock inconsistency; the fix is to thread the same injectable clock (wallClockNow, renamed/shared appropriately) through handleFrame and the View-layer calls (touch/dismiss/intentDidFinishPlaying) so SessionClient never reads a different clock than the one ConnectionManager uses for lifecycle-driven calls, and to narrow the :338 comment to describe only the two call sites it actually reaches (or complete the coverage) rather than claiming the general 'occurredAt/expiresAt/resume grace window' scope.

confirmed.title: 跨語言 fixture 對答案的 decideResumeBatch／budget.observing 在 App 內是死碼，出貨路徑另有一套手寫實作
confirmed.file: apps/interaction-ios/InteractionCompanion/Services/SessionReceive.swift:166 (observing) and :345 (decideResumeBatch definition; original citation of :346 is off by one line but same function)
confirmed.claim: `SessionDecisions.decideResumeBatch`（resume 批次的中止／跳過／上限規則）與 `SessionRealignBudget.observing`（有界 realign 預算）隨 App target 一起編譯出貨，但只有 ReceiveDecisionConformanceTests 會呼叫它們；production 的 `SessionClient.handleResponse`／`consume` 各自手寫了一份等價邏輯。因此 45 個 fixture 對到的是「批次與預算的參考實作」，而不是 App 真正跑的那條路，兩者一旦漂移沒有任何測試會紅。
confirmed.evidence: `rg 'observing\(|SessionResumeBatch|decideResumeBatch'` 在 apps/interaction-ios/ 底下只命中 SessionReceive.swift 的定義（:166、:196、:346-353）與 InteractionCompanionTests/ReceiveDecisionConformanceTests.swift:125、:188；InteractionCompanion/Services/SessionClient.swift 一次都沒有呼叫。production 的批次迴圈在 SessionClient.swift:888-899（自行判斷 `consume` 回傳值），上限檢查在 :874-887（自行呼叫 `resumeExceedsBound` 再 `sendSnapshotQuery`），預算則散在 :959（rejectInvalid）與 sendResume/sendSnapshotQuery 內的 `noteResumeAttempt`（:1155、:1175）。可觀察到的行為差異：`observing` 對任何 `.realign` 一律 `counting()`，而 production 只在 `transport.sendAip(envelope)` 真的回 true 時才記一次（SessionClient.swift:1151-1156），所以送出佇列滿／未連線時預算永遠不前進，`unrecoverable` 不會觸發，UI 一直停在「對齊中」。

verdicts.reasoning:
Verified the narrow, checkable part of the claim directly:

1. `rg 'decideResumeBatch|\.observing\('` across apps/interaction-ios/ shows both symbols defined only in SessionReceive.swift (:345 `decideResumeBatch`, :166 `observing`) and called only from InteractionCompanionTests/ReceiveDecisionConformanceTests.swift (:125, :152, :188, :452, :457). SessionClient.swift never references either name (confirmed with a second grep over its full call list of `SessionDecisions.*`).
2. SessionReceive.swift and ReceiveDecisionConformanceTests.swift are both brand-new files in this branch (`git show f5b8e2fc..:` reports "path does not exist" for both) — so this is squarely a defect introduced by the diff under review, not pre-existing.
3. SessionReceive.swift is compiled into the App target, not just the test target: the .xcodeproj uses `PBXFileSystemSynchronizedRootGroup` and the `InteractionCompanion` folder (containing Services/SessionReceive.swift) is owned by the `InteractionCompanion` app target, separate from the `InteractionCompanionTests` root group. So `decideResumeBatch`/`observing` do ship in the app binary as claimed, unreached by any app code path.
4. Production's hand-rolled equivalent is real and does diverge exactly as described: `consume()`/`handleResponse()` in SessionClient.swift loop over resume patches themselves (not via `decideResumeBatch`), and `noteResumeAttempt` is invoked from `sendResume`/`sendSnapshotQuery`/`failedToSync` — gated on `guard transport.sendAip(envelope) else { return }` (SessionClient.swift ~1151-1156, 1170-1179) — whereas `observing()`'s `.realign` branch counts unconditionally. This is a genuine, verified behavioral divergence between the two implementations.

However, the finding's consequence claim ("兩者一旦漂移沒有任何測試會紅" / "UI 一直停在對齊中") is overstated once you look past SessionReceive.swift/ReceiveDecisionConformanceTests.swift: apps/interaction-ios/InteractionCompanionTests/SessionClientTests.swift already contains a **pre-existing** (present in the base commit, untouched by this branch) test `testAResumeThatWasNeverSentIsNotCountedAsAnAttempt` that sets `transport.accepts = false`, drives `SessionSyncLocal.resumeFailureLimit + 2` failed sends, and explicitly asserts `client.syncStatus != .unrecoverable` and `!= .synced` — i.e. it directly pins down exactly the "queue full / never actually sent ⇒ don't count it, don't claim synced" behavior the finding calls a silent risk, against the real `SessionClient`, not the reference table. Likewise `testABoundaryRejectedAuthoritativeReplyCostsOneRealignAttempt` and `testAResumeReplyThatFailsHalfwayKeepsThePrefixAndAsksAgain` (both in the new ReceiveDecisionConformanceTests.swift, in its "客戶端行為（同一張表，走真的收訊路徑）" section) drive real `SessionClient.handleFrame` calls and assert the batch/reject-costs-one-attempt semantics production actually implements. So a regression in *production's own* budget/batch behavior would be caught — just not via the shared fixture, and not by comparing it against `observing()`/`decideResumeBatch`.

What survives scrutiny, and is the real, defensible core of the finding: the 45-case `receiveDecisions` fixture is sold (in the file's own header comment) as proving "同一則訊息，Rust／TypeScript／Swift 必須得到同一個決策", and the PR's stated goal (SessionClient.swift's new top-of-file comment) is "與權威實作的差異：**零**". But for the batch/budget dimensions specifically, the fixture only validates the standalone reference functions, which the app never calls — so if the shared fixture's `budgetAfter`/`applied`/`skipped` semantics evolve (as the Rust/TS canonical spec changes), Swift's fixture test will auto-track it while Swift's actual shipped `SessionClient` (hand-rolled, hardcoded-expectation tests) would not automatically be re-validated against the new spec values. That's a real, narrow conformance-testing gap distinct from "production has a live bug" — the app's actual behavior is independently well-tested, but the claimed 3-way conformance guarantee is not actually wired up for this slice of logic.

Net: the literal claim (dead code shipped in-binary, exercised only by tests, production hand-rolls a diverging equivalent) is fully verified. The scarier consequence framing is largely refuted by pre-existing, dedicated SessionClientTests.swift coverage of the exact scenarios cited as evidence — this isn't an untested landmine in shipped behavior, it's an unwired cross-language-conformance guarantee for two specific helper functions. That matches a low-severity, "known limitation / cleanup opportunity" finding rather than anything urgent.

confirmed.title: 「五個接線點」的第 4 點（scheduleRetry 的背景閘門）不可達，測試與 README 的枚舉不成立
confirmed.file: apps/interaction-ios/InteractionCompanion/Services/ConnectionManager.swift:875
confirmed.claim: ConnectionManagerGateTests.swift 檔頭與 apps/interaction-ios/README.md 都把「五個接線點」列成五件各自需要被驗過的事，但 `scheduleRetry()` 的唯一呼叫端就在 `handleConnectionLost()` 自己的背景閘門之後，且兩處在同一次同步呼叫中讀同一個 `lifecyclePhaseForGating()`，所以 :875 的 guard 永遠為真、永遠不會走進去。實際只有四個可達的接線點，而 `testALostConnectionInTheBackgroundDoesNotScheduleAReconnect` 斷言的 `pendingCount == 0` 由 :862 的閘門單獨保證，沒有任何測試能證明 :875 有效。
confirmed.evidence: `grep -n 'scheduleRetry()'` 只有兩行：:870（呼叫，位於 handleConnectionLost 內）與 :873（定義）。:862-869 `guard LifecycleDecision.shouldScheduleReconnect(phase: lifecyclePhaseForGating()) else { phase = .failed(...); return }` 先行返回，:870 才呼叫 scheduleRetry，:875 的同一個 guard 因此不可達。ConnectionManagerGateTests.swift:8-14 列出五點並在 :45 標「3＋4」由同一個測試涵蓋；apps/interaction-ios/README.md 新增段落稱這些閘門「都是**真的執行過**才通過的」。

verdicts.reasoning:
Verified directly against the current file contents (not stale).

1. Call graph: `grep -n 'scheduleRetry()'` across the whole iOS app (including tests) returns exactly two lines in ConnectionManager.swift — :870 (the call, inside `handleConnectionLost(reason:kind:)`) and :873 (the `private func` definition). No test or other production file calls `scheduleRetry()` directly (it's `private`), so `handleConnectionLost` is the sole entry point.

2. Same synchronous call, same input: `handleConnectionLost` reaches its own gate at :862 — `guard LifecycleDecision.shouldScheduleReconnect(phase: lifecyclePhaseForGating()) else { ...; return }` — and only on that guard passing does execution fall through to `scheduleRetry()` at :870, which re-runs the identical `guard LifecycleDecision.shouldScheduleReconnect(phase: lifecyclePhaseForGating()) else {...}` at :875. `shouldScheduleReconnect` (AppLifecycle.swift:139) is a pure function of its single argument (`phase != .background`), and `lifecyclePhaseForGating()` (ConnectionManager.swift:348) just reads `self.lifecyclePhase` with no side effects. Between the :862 check and the :875 check there is no `await`, no dispatch, and nothing else mutates `lifecyclePhase` (the intervening code — `cancelRetry()` — only clears the pending work item). So both guards evaluate the same input synchronously and must return the same boolean: if :862 passed (not background), :875 must also pass, making the `else` branch at :875-878 dead in every real call path.

3. Test evidence matches the claim exactly: `ConnectionManagerGateTests.swift` (added in this branch, commit a0d3309) enumerates the "five wiring points" at :8-14, explicitly labels point 4 `scheduleRetry()` as "同上（第二道）" (a second, redundant layer), and the test claimed to cover "3＋4" (`testALostConnectionInTheBackgroundDoesNotScheduleAReconnect`, :46-58) only ever triggers the background branch of `handleConnectionLost`, whose early `return` at :868 happens *before* `scheduleRetry()` is ever called — so the test cannot possibly exercise line 875's `else` branch; it only proves gate 3.

4. In-scope: `git diff f5b8e2fc9e86d8fa8067f91303dbbcb8d04cf42f..HEAD -- apps/interaction-ios/README.md` shows the "五個接線點" enumeration and the "都是**真的執行過**才通過的" sentence are new lines added on this branch (commit 1c8c2fa), and the test file itself is new on this branch (a0d3309). So this is a claim introduced by this branch's own diff, not pre-existing untouched code.

I could not find any way to make gate 4 reachable via the current call graph, nor any second caller, nor any state mutation between the two checks that would let them diverge. The finding's technical claim (unreachable guard, unproven "5th"/4th-listed point) holds up. Severity "low" is appropriate: it doesn't cause any incorrect production behavior (the redundant guard is harmless dead code, and behavior is still correct because the outer gate at :862 already does the real work) — it's a doc/test-honesty overclaim (the enumeration in the test header and README overstates how many *independently reachable* points were exercised), which matters given this project's explicit 誠實階梯 emphasis on test/coverage honesty, but is not a functional/safety bug.

confirmed.fix: 移除 :874-878 的重複 guard（或把 :862 的早退改成直接呼叫 scheduleRetry 讓 :875 成為唯一決策點），並把測試檔頭與 README 的「五個接線點」改成實際可達的四個。

Two honest options: (a) collapse the redundant gate — remove the guard at ConnectionManager.swift:862 (or the one at :875) so `handleConnectionLost` unconditionally calls `scheduleRetry()`, which becomes the single real gate; add a XCTest asserting `scheduler.pendingCount == 0` after a background disconnect (already exists) plus a coverage-style test that forces `lifecyclePhaseForGating` to flip between the two checks (would require making scheduleRetry's phase check meaningfully independent, e.g. by re-reading phase at actual timer-fire time only, matching what point 5 already does) — or (b) leave the defensive duplicate guard as intentional belt-and-suspenders, but correct ConnectionManagerGateTests.swift's header and README.md's "五個接線點...都是真的執行過" wording to say four independently-reachable gates plus one intentionally-redundant defensive check, so the test-count claim matches what the tests actually exercise.

confirmed.evidence: declarative_lifecycle.rs:346-360 `tokio::spawn` + `timeout_at(deadline, run_declarative_rebind(...))`，逾時只產生 `RebindStop::Failed("the rebind exceeded its bounded budget")`；declarative_lifecycle.rs:579-608 是關鍵區段：`unregister_receptor`（585-591）→ `register_declarative_spec`（596-598，內部 providers.rs:792-794 是一個帶 `.await?` 的逐項迴圈，可被中途 drop）→ 599-607 的 `set_receptor_enabled(&id, false)` 還原迴圈 → 608 `clear_declarative_human_disabled`。declarative_lifecycle.rs:409-438 的失敗處理只做 `settle_declarative_rebind(false)`＋`note_provider_rebind_failed`＋稽核，沒有把能力旗標帶回停用前的樣子。誠實界線：我沒有構造出一個實際的時序（步驟 1-5 上限約 3 s drain + 2.5 s STOP_SENSORS_WAIT，registry 操作很快，所以 40 s 預算通常會落在步驟 7 後半那個安全的握手輪詢迴圈裡）；`lock_provider`（registry/providers.rs:212-226）沒有逾時、會排在同一台 provider 的其他決定後面，是唯一能把時間推到關鍵區段裡的變數。

verdicts.reasoning:
Verified the mechanism directly against the current file content (this whole module is new in this branch — it does not exist at base f5b8e2f — so it is squarely in scope).

1. `spawn_declarative_rebind` (declarative_lifecycle.rs:346-360) wraps the *entire* `run_declarative_rebind(...)` future in `tokio::time::timeout_at(now+40s, ...)`. `tokio::time::Timeout::poll` polls the inner future once per wake; if that poll returns `Pending` and the deadline has already passed, it returns `Err(Elapsed)` and drops the inner future wherever it was last suspended — this is exactly how `timeout_at` behaves, so the "can be dropped at any await point" premise is correct.

2. The critical section (lines 590-608, confirmed by direct read) is exactly as described:
   - `human_disabled` is snapshotted at line 595.
   - `rt.register_declarative_spec(&spec).await` (596-598) internally calls `providers.rs:777-782`'s `self.registry.register_receptor(receptor).await?` in a loop; `interaction-registry/src/lib.rs:114-133` sets `enabled: !manifest.requires_consent` — i.e. any non-consent receptor comes back **enabled by default**, unconditionally, including ones a human had previously turned off.
   - Only *after* that full await returns does the loop at 599-605 walk `human_disabled` and call `set_receptor_enabled(&id, false)` to restore the human's choice, and only after *that* loop finishes does line 608 clear the `human_disabled` record.
   - I confirmed via `interaction-registry/src/lib.rs:196-201` (`receptor()`) that the `enabled` flag is the real gate used for actual data access (not just a display flag) — `receptor()` returns `Unavailable` when disabled and the live instance when enabled — so a receptor left wrongly `enabled` is not merely a cosmetic state.
   - I confirmed the failure path (`fail_declarative_rebind` → `note_provider_rebind_failed`, providers.rs:1457-1483) only rewrites the provider's `detail`/warnings via `transition(id, existing.state, ...)`; it never touches receptor/actuator `enabled` flags. There is no `Drop`-guard or other compensation anywhere in `declarative_lifecycle.rs`/`providers.rs` for this path (grepped for `Drop`/`Guard`; none present). So the claim "timeout path never rolls back" is accurate.
   - This directly contradicts the guarantee the same module's own comment states at lines 592-594 ("既有保證：回到 Available 不自動恢復任何能力") and the CHANGELOG's own claim for commit `9799b1e` ("rebind 不得打開人類手動關掉的受器").

3. I tried hard to find a reason this can't actually happen (to refute it):
   - All of the sub-`.await`s inside the critical window (`register_receptor`/`unregister_receptor`/`set_receptor_enabled`) are `tokio::sync::RwLock` writes on in-memory maps that resolve immediately when uncontended — Rust's generated async state machine does not yield to the executor across a `.await` that resolves `Ready` synchronously, so under zero contention this whole burst runs inside one poll and the `Timeout` wrapper gets no chance to interleave mid-burst.
   - However, the registry's receptor/actuator maps are *shared across all providers* (a single `RwLock<HashMap<...>>>`, not per-provider), so a genuinely concurrent write from an unrelated provider's registration/transition happening at the same instant is a real, if narrow, source of a `Pending` yield exactly inside this window.
   - Earlier steps (drain ≤3s, `stop_provider_sensing` ≤~2-5s bounded by `STOP_SENSORS_WAIT`) leave large slack in the 40s budget under normal conditions; the only unbounded variable is `lock_provider(&id).await` contention from a concurrent `transition_provider`/`revoke_provider` decision on the *same* provider — and those paths are themselves bounded to a few seconds, not tens of seconds. So hitting the exact window (near-exhausted budget AND contention landing inside the 599-605 loop) requires several independent low-probability conditions to align. I could not construct nor rule out a concrete reproducing timeline, matching the original finder's own honesty boundary.
   - I also checked that `bind_declarative_device` (called inside `register_declarative_spec`) does `tokio::spawn(binding.run())` for the physical device-link tasks — these are detached and keep running even if the outer `run_declarative_rebind` future is dropped, so a receptor left wrongly `enabled` by this race is not necessarily inert: the underlying transport can still come up in the background while nothing observes it to converge `ProviderState` to `Available`, meaning `registry.receptor(id)` could actually serve real data for a receptor a human disabled, for a bounded window until the CHANGELOG-documented backoff supervisor retries the rebind (which re-runs unregister→register→restore using the still-intact `human_disabled` record, self-healing it).

No test exists covering this specific cancellation window (grepped `providers_loop.rs`/`mqtt_rebind_loop.rs`/`declarative_session_loop.rs` for `kept_disabled`/timeout/cancel — none), so this is not "already covered" nor "already fixed" (the file is new; there is no earlier version to have drifted from). This is a real, narrow, self-healing-on-next-retry-but-real cancel-safety gap, correctly self-assessed as low severity by the original finder. I'm confirming it at the same "low" severity rather than upgrading or downgrading, since the mechanism is real but the exposure window is narrow and self-correcting.

confirmed.fix: 不要用 timeout_at 包住整段：把總預算改成只套在會卡住的那幾步（drain、握手輪詢），或在關鍵區段外圍放一個 drop guard／補償步驟，讓被取消時仍然把 `human_disabled` 名單重新套回去（紀錄本來就刻意保留到套用成功才清）。至少替 `set_receptor_enabled` 失敗的那幾個受器留稽核，別讓 `keptDisabledReceptors: []` 同時代表「沒有這種受器」與「沒關成功」。
confirmed.regressionTest: Hard to hit deterministically without adding a test seam, since the race depends on the shared registry RwLock being contended at exactly the wrong instant, or on `lock_provider` contention consuming nearly all of the 40s budget. A practical regression test: (1) add a test-only hook (e.g. a `tokio::sync::Notify`/oneshot gate reachable only under `#[cfg(test)]`) that pauses `run_declarative_rebind` right after `register_declarative_spec(...).await` returns and right before the `human_disabled` restore loop; (2) in the test, disable a non-consent receptor via `transition`/`set_receptor_enabled(false)` to seed `human_disabled`; (3) trigger a rebind, let it pause at the hook, and from the test thread abort/drop the task's `JoinHandle` (simulating the `timeout_at` cancellation) instead of resuming it; (4) assert `registry.receptor_flags(&id)` still reports `enabled=false` for the previously-disabled receptor — this should fail on current code (receptor comes back enabled) and pass once a scope-guard/rollback is added around the register→restore sequence so cancellation between them re-closes whatever was just opened.
